mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Create a discreet exterior identity, professional reception and clear appointment directions. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discuss room privacy and visitor routes without adding unnecessary personal or case information to displays. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: A recognisable shopfront brings your name, window display and customer entrance together. We help retailers balance permanent branding with promotions that change, so the business remains easy to spot while the offer stays fresh. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Customers should understand what you sell before reaching the door. Give the business name a clear position, use the glass selectively and reserve a separate area for seasonal messages. Inside, consistent department and collection signs help the visit feel straightforward. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Help customers recognise your speciality with shopfront branding, product displays and clear collection information. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Separate your permanent name from products, prices and offers that change through the week. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Connect the roadside entrance with plant departments, outdoor displays and the checkout. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a consistent hierarchy across exposed outdoor positions and sheltered retail spaces. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Introduce kitchens, bathrooms or interiors with strong exterior branding and coordinated product-zone graphics. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give each display area a clear identity while allowing room for product ranges to change. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Express the personality of your shop through a fascia, considered window lettering and a clear entrance. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep the permanent identity separate from changing window displays and weekly promotions. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Education signage has to work for new families, pupils, staff and visiting organisations. A clear entrance, consistent building names and understandable directions help the site feel welcoming and organised. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan signs around the different users of the site. Reception visitors, deliveries and everyday arrivals may follow separate routes. Agree the wording and naming with the school or provider, then give each message a clear place in the overall system. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sport and leisure signage brings a venue’s identity into entrances, reception areas and activity spaces. We help connect the energy of the brand with practical information that makes the venue easier to use. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Think about first-time visitors as well as regular members. They need to recognise the entrance, find check-in and understand where their activity begins. Event-day and everyday routes may differ, so temporary information should have a defined place. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

mainEntity.name: Which signs should we start with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visitors often arrive somewhere unfamiliar. Clear signage helps them recognise the destination, find reception and move confidently through the property. We bring the identity of accommodation and attractions into exterior signs, room information and visitor displays. Start with the main identity, then identify any point where customers or visitors need another instruction. The starter package above is a starting point for that discussion.

mainEntity.name: Can we update existing signs rather than replace everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, send photographs of the items you want to retain, along with original artwork if available. We can discuss replacement graphics, matching finishes or a phased refresh. The condition and construction of existing signs will affect what can be reused.

mainEntity.name: What should we send for a quotation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at the whole arrival sequence: approach, entrance, reception and the final destination. Each point needs the right amount of information. A strong main sign cannot compensate for an unclear turn or a reception door that looks like a private entrance. Include your premises postcode, approximate sizes, photographs, logo files and the date you are working towards. Mention whether you need design, delivery or installation so the quote describes the full requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with design and fitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can discuss design, manufacture and installation as part of the project. Artwork is reviewed before production, and any survey or fitting requirements are agreed for the actual address. Supply approved wording for specialist or operational signs and any landlord or site requirements.

mainEntity.name: How long will the project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The schedule depends on the sign types, quantities, material availability and fitting arrangements. Tell us your opening or event date at the outset. We agree the programme around approved artwork, any required permissions and the readiness of the premises rather than applying one lead time to every job.

Landlord approval, advertisement consent and any highway or listed-building considerations should be confirmed by the relevant parties before production.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="checklist"><div class="wrap"><h2>Let’s get your project started.</h2><div class="split"><div><p>Send the details below to our Norwich team. We will discuss the specification, artwork and completion date before preparing your quotation.</p><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Photographs looking along both directions of the street</li><li>Proposed position, approximate size and wall details</li><li>Any planning conditions, landlord approval and lighting requirements</li></ul></div><div><h3>From brief to finished display.</h3><ol><li>Share your requirements, photographs and intended date.</li><li>Agree the quoted items, material specification and delivery or fitting arrangements.</li><li>Check the artwork, wording and dimensions before approving production.</li><li>Arrange collection, delivery or installation as agreed.</li></ol><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">Discuss projecting signs ↗</a></div></div></div></section><section class="section" id="faq"><div class="wrap"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Can the sign be printed on both sides?</summary><p>Yes, a double-sided layout can address people approaching from either direction. The artwork and mounting orientation are agreed together.</p></details><details><summary>Do projecting signs need permission?</summary><p>The answer depends on the proposal and location. Check the relevant local authority and landlord requirements before manufacture.</p></details><details><summary>Can we reuse an existing bracket?</summary><p>Send photographs and dimensions. Reuse depends on its condition, capacity and suitability for the new sign, and needs assessment before it is included in a quotation.</p></details></div></section><section class="section tint" id="advice"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs"><img alt="Do you need planning consent for a shop sign? signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/planning-consent-for-shop-signs.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Do you need planning consent for a shop sign? ↗</h3></a><p>Understand advertisement consent in England, what to check with your council and how to prepare a clear shop-sign brief before production.</p></article><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/compare/illuminated-vs-non-illuminated-shop-signs"><img alt="Illuminated vs non-illuminated shop signs signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/illuminated-vs-non-illuminated-shop-signs.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Illuminated vs non-illuminated shop signs ↗</h3></a><p>Choose lighting around when customers arrive, how your frontage is seen and what the building allows. Compare appearance, maintenance, installation and the cost of operating the complete sign.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="section" id="related"><div class="wrap"><h2>Explore related signage.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/built-up-3d-letters"><img alt="Brushed-metal built-up 3D letters with halo lighting on a dark building front" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/services/built-up-3d-letters-norwich.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Built-up 3D letters ↗</h3></a><p>Give your name and logo a three-dimensional finish with individually fabricated letters for shopfronts, offices and reception areas. We help you choose the scale, finish and mounting around the building and the way people approach it.</p></article><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/fascia-signs"><img alt="Purple shop fascia sign above a traditional stone shopfront" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/services/fascia-signs-norwich.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Fascia signs ↗</h3></a><p>Shop and building fascia signs designed around your brand, frontage and viewing distance. Bring your name, logo and key information together in a layout that is easy to recognise.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="norwich"><div class="wrap"><h2>Talk to our Norwich team.</h2><div class="split"><p>Visit Broadland Digital at Vulcan House, Vulcan Road North, Norwich, NR6 6AQ. Arrange a conversation about your project, materials and artwork, or send your photographs by email to get started.</p><div><a class="button" href="tel:01603407786">Call 01603 407786 ↗</a> <a class="button" href="mailto:production@broadlanddigital.co.uk">Email the team ↗</a><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Plan your visit ↗</a></p></div></div></div></section></main><section class="section tint crm-enquiry" id="enquiry"><div class="wrap"><h2>Discuss a project.</h2><p>Tell us about your premises, the signs you need and the date you are working towards. Send photographs and approximate sizes if you have them.</p><div class="actions"><a class="button purple" href="tel:01603407786">CALL 01603 407786</a> <a class="button" href="mailto:production@broadlanddigital.co.uk">EMAIL PRODUCTION@BROADLANDDIGITAL.CO.UK</a></div><p class="small">Broadland Digital, Vulcan House, Vulcan Road North, Norwich, NR6 6AQ · Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5pm</p></div></section></div>

mainEntity.name: Is premium print sharper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. Print quality depends on the artwork, media and production specification. The premium description may refer mainly to the stand hardware. Compare these items separately.

mainEntity.name: Can I use it outside?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if the exact product is designed and specified for that environment. Ordinary indoor pull-up banners are not a substitute for an appropriate outdoor display, even when placed near an entrance.

mainEntity.name: Can I change the graphic myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on the model. Some replacements require specialist fitting and spring mechanisms should not be dismantled casually. Ask for the approved process before buying.

mainEntity.name: Would a pop-up display be better?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a broader backdrop or a coordinated exhibition presence, it may be worth comparing. Start with the available stand space, transport and setup arrangements, then choose the format that supports your message.

Either can look considered and professional when the scale, typography and installation suit the building.</p><p>The best starting point is a photograph of the whole frontage. returns that create depth. It differs from flat-cut lettering, which is cut from a sheet and may be mounted directly or on spacers. Architectural lettering can combine different materials, finishes and illuminated effects. The exact construction should be chosen to suit the artwork and installation.</p><p>The appeal is often the way individual letters sit on the building, cast shadows and create a substantial identity without filling the whole fascia with one printed rectangle. This can work well for simple wordmarks with generous spacing. A logo with many small separate elements may need simplification or a supporting panel so the installation remains coherent.</p><p>Potential limits include fabrication complexity, alignment, the suitability of narrow strokes and the number of fixing points. The wall behind the letters becomes part of the design. Existing holes, discolouration or uneven surfaces will not necessarily disappear. Include preparation or making good in the brief rather than discovering it after the old sign has been removed.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="panels"><h2>Flat panels: a clear canvas for the whole message.</h2><p>A flat panel establishes its own background, making it useful when the brand relies on a strong colour field, a detailed logo or a secondary line of text. It can also create a consistent visual area across an otherwise busy frontage. The panel material and edge treatment influence the finish, so compare more than the artwork alone.</p><p>Aluminium composite is one possible substrate. The <a href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/by-brand/dibond-r/">DIBOND manufacturer page</a> explains the aluminium-skin composite construction and its use in signage. That does not mean every flat panel should use the same sheet: dimensions, environment, support and any project requirements need to determine the specification.</p><p>The main limitation is that a large continuous surface can look visually heavy if its proportion and layout are poorly judged. Panel joins, exposed fixings and edges also need deliberate treatment. A panel should not be used to conceal an unsound mounting surface. If the wall or fascia needs repair, address that before fitting the new sign.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="hybrid"><h2>You can combine both approaches.</h2><p>The choice is not always either letters or a panel. Raised or built-up lettering can be mounted onto a designed background, creating depth while controlling the colour behind it. This can be helpful where the building surface is visually inconsistent or where a complete branded fascia is wanted.</p><p>A hybrid needs a clear purpose. Adding layers solely because more components seem more impressive can increase cost without improving the sign. Ask whether the background is solving a contrast issue, providing a neat mounting arrangement or establishing the right shape for the frontage. If it is doing none of those things, a simpler composition may be stronger.</p><p>Flat-cut acrylic lettering offers another comparison when some dimension is wanted without the same fabricated construction. The thickness, fixing method and viewing distance determine its effect. Discuss a sample of the proposed letter, including its edge and mounting, so you are comparing the finished result rather than two very different render styles.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="artwork"><h2>Typography can decide which construction works best.</h2><p>Bring the original vector logo if you have it. Screen images can show the appearance, but production planning needs accurate outlines and proportions. Ask how fine strokes, small enclosed shapes and separate punctuation will be made and fixed. A logo designed for stationery may need a considered signage version rather than a direct enlargement.</p><p>For panels, keep the message disciplined even though the entire surface is printable. A fascia is usually there to identify the business, not reproduce every service in a brochure. If a strapline is useful, test it at the actual viewing distance. Opening hours or detailed offers can often sit elsewhere in the customer journey.</p><p>For individual letters, check the spacing as a complete word rather than inspecting each character alone. The apparent gaps around different letter shapes can vary. Request a proof showing the entire installation and its relationship to windows, doors and fascia edges. This is especially useful when the business name includes both wide and narrow characters.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="installation"><h2>The building and access affect both options.</h2><p>Built-up lettering typically needs careful setting out, while a panel needs an appropriate support and fixing arrangement across its size. Neither should be designed independently of the building. Tell us about cladding, render, brickwork, existing fascia boards and any areas the landlord says must not be drilled.</p><p>Access can be a significant part of the project. A sign above a canopy or close to a busy entrance may require different arrangements from a low-level installation with clear space. Agree the working area, customer access and timing before promising an opening date. Removal of the old sign and making good should be included explicitly.</p><p>If illumination is being considered, assess it as a separate design and installation decision. Some built-up letters can house lighting; other schemes use external lighting. Flat signs can also be illuminated in appropriate ways. Read our <a href="/signage-home/compare/illuminated-vs-non-illuminated-shop-signs">illuminated versus non-illuminated comparison</a> before assuming that choosing dimensional letters commits you to a lit sign.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="scenarios"><h2>Examples of a useful match between format and business.</h2><p>Illustrative example: a design studio has a simple wordmark and a clean, well-maintained wall. Individual built-up letters could let the architecture remain visible while giving the name depth. The proposal should show how the smaller descriptor is handled and whether the chosen contrast remains clear from the pavement.</p><p>Illustrative example: a trade counter needs its name and a concise description to be unmistakable across a yard. A flat panel with strong contrast may provide a direct, readable solution. The panel layout can establish a clear brand block without asking individual small letters to compete with the building cladding.</p><p>Illustrative example: a salon replaces an old fascia with visible repairs beneath it. A designed background with raised lettering may be worth comparing with a straightforward panel. The final choice should follow a surface inspection and a costed proposal for making good, rather than relying on a mock-up that hides the building condition.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="updates"><h2>Think about the next change before ordering.</h2><p>If the name, strapline or tenant is likely to change, ask how the chosen sign could be updated. A panel graphic may be replaceable in some specifications; individual letters may leave fixing points when removed. Neither option should be promised as a universal quick change. Record the material, dimensions and installation details for future work.</p><p>For external proposals, check approvals before manufacture. <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/outdoor-advertisements-and-signs-a-guide-for-advertisers">Government guidance on outdoor signs</a> explains the advertisement-control system in England. The choice of lettering or panel alone does not determine consent. Position, scale, site context and any lighting all need to be considered with the relevant authority.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="checklist"><h2>Your project checklist.</h2><ul class="project-checklist"><li>A full frontage photograph and close-ups of the existing sign.</li><li>Available width, height and approximate installation position.</li><li>Original logo files, preferred colours and any secondary wording.</li><li>Whether the building background should remain visible.</li><li>Known wall condition, landlord constraints and access arrangements.</li><li>Daytime or evening viewing needs and whether lighting is required.</li><li>Expected future changes to the name, tenant or supporting message.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">TALK THROUGH YOUR PROJECT ↗</a></p></section><section class="reading-section" id="faq"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Are built-up letters always more expensive?</summary><p>They often involve more fabrication and setting out, but a useful comparison needs the same size and installation scope. A large complex panel installation may cost more than a modest lettering scheme. Request a project-specific breakdown.</p></details><details><summary>Are flat-cut letters the same as built-up letters?</summary><p>No. Flat-cut letters are cut from sheet material. Built-up letters have a fabricated depth with faces and returns. Both can provide dimension, but their edge appearance, fixing and lighting possibilities differ.</p></details><details><summary>Can a panel look premium?</summary><p>Yes. Proportion, material selection, colour, typography and neat installation matter more than the label. A carefully detailed panel can be a better result than unsuitable dimensional lettering.</p></details><details><summary>Can you match an existing sign?</summary><p>Send photographs, dimensions and any original specification. A close match may require samples and inspection. Existing weathering and discontinued materials can affect how a new component sits alongside the old work.</p></details></section><section class="reading-section" id="sources"><h2>Sources & further reading.</h2><p class="source-note">Sources checked for this draft on 18 October 2026. Product ratings apply to the stated product and test conditions; confirm the current specification for your order.</p><ul class="source-links"><li><a class="" href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/by-brand/dibond-r/">DIBOND sheet information ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/outdoor-advertisements-and-signs-a-guide-for-advertisers">Outdoor advertisements and signs ↗</a></li></ul></section><section class="reading-section" id="services"><h2>Put the advice into practice.</h2><p>Tell us where the sign will go, what it needs to communicate and the date you are working towards. Our Norwich team can discuss the design, materials and fitting around your project.</p><div class="service-links"><a class="button" href="/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs">Built-up 3D letters ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs">Fascia signs ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/laser-cutting-engraving">Laser-cut acrylic signs ↗</a></div><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Visit our Norwich workshop ↗</a> · <a class="" href="/sectors">Find signage for your sector ↗</a></p></section></article></div><section class="section tint"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid research-cards"><article class="card" data-search="Illuminated vs non-illuminated shop signs Choose lighting around when customers arrive, how your frontage is seen and what the building allows. Compare appearance, maintenance, installation and the cost of operating the complete sign."><a href="/signage-home/compare/illuminated-vs-non-illuminated-shop-signs"><img alt="Illuminated vs non-illuminated shop signs — signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/illuminated-vs-non-illuminated-shop-signs.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Illuminated vs non-illuminated shop signs ↗</h3></a><p>Choose lighting around when customers arrive, how your frontage is seen and what the building allows. Compare appearance, maintenance, installation and the cost of operating the complete sign.</p></article><article class="card" data-search="Foamex vs aluminium composite vs Correx Choose a board around its setting, support and useful working life. Compare rigid PVC, aluminium composite and fluted polypropylene for indoor displays, outdoor branding and temporary site information."><a href="/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx"><img alt="Foamex vs aluminium composite vs Correx — signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Foamex vs aluminium composite vs Correx ↗</h3></a><p>Choose a board around its setting, support and useful working life. Compare rigid PVC, aluminium composite and fluted polypropylene for indoor displays, outdoor branding and temporary site information.</p></article><article class="card" data-search="PVC vs mesh banners A solid banner gives you a continuous print surface. Choosing the most expensive sheet for every application is rarely necessary; choosing the cheapest without considering the installation can also create avoidable replacement work.</p><p>Begin with three questions: where will the board go, how will it be supported, and how long will the message remain relevant? A sign with a changing date has a different replacement cycle from your business name. Tell us whether people will inspect it at arm’s length or read it across a yard. We can then compare complete specifications, including print, finish, fittings and installation, rather than judging materials by a sample thickness alone.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="at-a-glance"><h2>Compare at a glance.</h2><p class="table-hint">On a smaller screen, scroll across to compare all options.</p><div aria-label="Foamex vs aluminium composite vs Correx comparison table" class="comparison-scroll" role="region" tabindex="0"><table><caption>Foamex vs aluminium composite vs Correx at a glance</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Factor</th><th scope="col">Foamex / foam PVC</th><th scope="col">Aluminium composite</th><th scope="col">Correx</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Typical starting point</th><td>Supported indoor graphics</td><td>Lasting exterior identity</td><td>Temporary campaign boards</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Construction</th><td>Rigid foam PVC sheet</td><td>Aluminium skins around a core</td><td>Fluted polypropylene sheet</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Close viewing</th><td>Smooth face; inspect exposed edges</td><td>Flat face; tidy edge planning matters</td><td>Flutes can influence appearance</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Support</th><td>Specify backing and fixings</td><td>Specify fixing structure and spacing</td><td>Plan ties, holes and frame support</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Transport</th><td>Protect face and corners</td><td>Protect against dents and edge damage</td><td>Avoid crushing and bending</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Outdoor selection</th><td>Check exact grade and exposure</td><td>Check exact grade and installation</td><td>Match short-term use and exposure</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Changing message</th><td>Reprint or replace to suit campaign</td><td>Consider whether updates justify specification</td><td>Useful to consider for frequent replacement</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Buying priority</th><td>Finished appearance and support</td><td>Whole installation and long-term brief</td><td>Clear message and proportionate specification</td></tr></tbody></table></div></section><section class="reading-section" id="foamex"><h2>Foamex: useful for smooth, lightweight displays.</h2><p>Foamex is a name commonly used in UK signage for rigid foam PVC sheet. It is not the paper-faced foamboard used for some presentation mounts. Manufacturer ranges such as <a href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/by-brand/forex-r/">3A Composites FOREX</a> illustrate this material family; the actual brand, grade and thickness should be stated in your quotation.</p><p>Consider it for indoor information boards, retail displays and wall-mounted graphics where a smooth printed face matters. A modest panel supported against a suitable wall is a different proposition from a large sheet spanning between posts. The layout of the fixings and the backing can be as important as the nominal thickness. For shaped graphics, discuss the outline and narrow sections before artwork is finished.</p><p>Its limitations deserve attention when the board will be outdoors, exposed to heat, knocked during handling or left unsupported. Do not assume all foam PVC is suitable for every external location. Request a grade-specific recommendation and agree how expansion, fixings and exposed edges will be accommodated. If a pristine edge is central to a premium reception installation, compare a physical sample with the alternatives.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="composite"><h2>Aluminium composite: a strong candidate for lasting exterior branding.</h2><p>Aluminium composite material, often abbreviated to ACM, combines aluminium outer skins with a core. It is not a solid aluminium plate. <a href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/by-brand/dibond-r/">DIBOND manufacturer information</a> describes its sheet as rigid and suitable for indoor and outdoor applications. Generic ACM products differ, so the name alone does not establish the exact specification.</p><p>For workshop identification, business park panels or a long-term fascia face, ACM is often worth comparing first. Its flat appearance suits clean lettering and broad colour areas. However, a flat sheet still needs an appropriate fixing arrangement. The building substrate, panel dimensions, access and exposure should determine the installation, rather than copying the fixing pattern from an unrelated sign.</p><p>The initial material cost may be higher than a temporary board solution, and damaged corners or dents can undermine the finish. Consider protective handling and installation access early. Different cores, coatings and grades are available; do not treat a general signage sheet as a substitute for a specified building or fire-performance product. Where a project has formal performance requirements, obtain the exact product documentation before approval.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="correx"><h2>Correx: practical when the message is temporary.</h2><p>Correx is a branded fluted polypropylene sheet manufactured by <a href="https://corplex.com/">Corplex</a>. The hollow fluted construction differs visibly from solid-looking foam PVC and aluminium composite. It is useful to consider when the sign needs to be light, easy to distribute and proportionate to a short campaign.</p><p>Temporary event directions, changing construction notices and promotional boards are good starting points for discussion. Think about whether the board will be tied to a fence, mounted to a frame or placed into a purpose-made holder. Flute direction, hole positions and the contact area around each fixing affect how the panel behaves; simply pulling cable ties tighter is not a substitute for choosing a suitable fixing arrangement.</p><p>Correx is less suited to briefs where a perfectly smooth premium face or a substantial exposed edge is the main goal. A board that performs well for temporary instructions can look out of place as the principal sign on a carefully finished shopfront. It should also not be described as universally recyclable without checking how the printed and fitted finished board will actually be collected locally.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="installation"><h2>Compare installed signs, not loose sheets.</h2><p>Ask for the same finished size, artwork coverage and fixing scope in each quotation. One price may include drilled holes and another only the printed board. One may include a site survey, removal of an existing panel and installation; another may be collection only. Separate these items so you can see which difference comes from the material and which comes from the work needed to put it in place.</p><p>Photographs should show the entire installation area and a closer view of the mounting surface. Mention brick, render, cladding, fencing or a freestanding frame. Avoid drilling or climbing to gather information: approximate measurements from a safe position are enough for an initial conversation. Final fabrication dimensions and fixing details may need a survey.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="scenarios"><h2>Three example briefs, three different priorities.</h2><p>Illustrative example: a Norwich retailer needs a seasonal offer board inside a window. The message changes frequently, customers stand close to it and the display is supported. A smooth foam PVC board is worth assessing, with attention to sunlight, glare and the chosen holder. There is little value in specifying a heavier permanent installation solely because it sounds more robust.</p><p>Illustrative example: an engineering company wants its name above a yard entrance. The artwork is unlikely to change and the sign represents the business every working day. Compare an ACM panel with a properly planned installation. A temporary campaign board might reduce the purchase price but would not necessarily meet the desired appearance or support requirements.</p><p>Illustrative example: an organiser needs a set of arrows for a one-day event. Lightweight Correx may suit the temporary message and distribution plan, provided positioning, fixing and removal are agreed. Direction arrows need to be checked individually against the actual route; printing the same arrow on every panel can create confusion on site.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="artwork"><h2>Make the graphic work at its actual viewing distance.</h2><p>Board choice cannot rescue a crowded design. Give the main message enough space, use clear contrast and decide what can be read from the intended approach. A road-facing panel needs a shorter message than a reception information board. Ask for a proof that shows the finished panel shape and any holes, with essential text clear of the fixing zones.</p><p>If several boards form a larger display, agree the panel joins before production. Keep important letters and faces away from awkward seams where possible. Ask how replacement panels would be matched later, especially if a campaign may expand. Retain the approved artwork and specification so a future reorder starts with the correct size and material.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="decision"><h2>Our practical starting point.</h2><p>For a smooth supported indoor display, start the discussion with foam PVC. For lasting exterior identity, compare aluminium composite. For temporary directions and short campaigns, consider Correx. These are useful starting points rather than blanket rules. The right recommendation comes from the combination of environment, finished dimensions, mounting and the standard of appearance you want.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="checklist"><h2>Your project checklist.</h2><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Finished width and height, quantity and whether each board differs.</li><li>Indoor or outdoor position, photographs and the intended viewing distance.</li><li>Expected campaign duration and how often the wording changes.</li><li>Mounting surface or frame, access restrictions and existing fixings.</li><li>Single or double-sided artwork, shape and any drilled holes.</li><li>Required collection, delivery or fitting date and a realistic budget range.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">TALK THROUGH YOUR PROJECT ↗</a></p></section><section class="reading-section" id="faq"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Is thicker always better?</summary><p>No. Thickness is only one part of the specification. A smaller well-supported panel can behave differently from a larger unsupported one. Compare the exact material and fixing arrangement rather than choosing by thickness alone.</p></details><details><summary>Can I use the same artwork on all three?</summary><p>Usually the design can be adapted, but the final proof should match the actual panel dimensions, shape and fixing areas. Colours and surface appearance can differ, so request a sample if brand matching is particularly important.</p></details><details><summary>Which lasts longest?</summary><p>There is no reliable universal lifespan without knowing the product, print system, exposure and installation. Tell us the intended service period and ask for a recommendation based on the complete sign.</p></details><details><summary>Can existing fixings be reused?</summary><p>Possibly, after their position and condition have been checked. A new panel can have different support needs. Send photographs, but allow for inspection before treating the old installation as suitable.</p></details></section><section class="reading-section" id="sources"><h2>Sources & further reading.</h2><p class="source-note">Sources checked for this draft on 18 October 2026. Product ratings apply to the stated product and test conditions; confirm the current specification for your order.</p><ul class="source-links"><li><a class="" href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/by-brand/forex-r/">FOREX rigid foam PVC ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/by-brand/dibond-r/">DIBOND aluminium composite ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://corplex.com/">Corplex, manufacturer of Correx ↗</a></li></ul></section><section class="reading-section" id="services"><h2>Put the advice into practice.</h2><p>Tell us where the sign will go, what it needs to communicate and the date you are working towards. Our Norwich team can discuss the design, materials and fitting around your project.</p><div class="service-links"><a class="button" href="/signage-home/large-format-print">Foamex boards ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/large-format-print">Aluminium composite panels ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/large-format-print">Correx boards ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/site-safety-signs">Construction site boards ↗</a></div><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Visit our Norwich workshop ↗</a> · <a class="" href="/sectors">Find signage for your sector ↗</a></p></section></article></div><section class="section tint"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid research-cards"><article class="card" data-search="PVC vs mesh banners A solid banner gives you a continuous print surface. Mesh introduces openings that change both the graphic and the installation conversation. Choose around the position, exposure and message."><a href="/signage-home/compare/pvc-vs-mesh-banners"><img alt="PVC vs mesh banners — signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/pvc-vs-mesh-banners.webp" width="1600"/><h3>PVC vs mesh banners ↗</h3></a><p>A solid banner gives you a continuous print surface. Mesh introduces openings that change both the graphic and the installation conversation. Choose around the position, exposure and message.</p></article><article class="card" data-search="Built-up letters vs flat panel signs Decide whether your frontage needs dimensional lettering, a continuous branded face or a combination. Compare visual impact, artwork, mounting, updating and installation."><a href="/signage-home/compare/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs"><img alt="Built-up letters vs flat panel signs — signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Built-up letters vs flat panel signs ↗</h3></a><p>Decide whether your frontage needs dimensional lettering, a continuous branded face or a combination. acceptedAnswer.text: No. Thickness is only one part of the specification. A smaller well-supported panel can behave differently from a larger unsupported one. Compare the exact material and fixing arrangement rather than choosing by thickness alone.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the same artwork on all three?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually the design can be adapted, but the final proof should match the actual panel dimensions, shape and fixing areas. Colours and surface appearance can differ, so request a sample if brand matching is particularly important.

mainEntity.name: Which lasts longest?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no reliable universal lifespan without knowing the product, print system, exposure and installation. Tell us the intended service period and ask for a recommendation based on the complete sign.

mainEntity.name: Can existing fixings be reused?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly, after their position and condition have been checked. A new panel can have different support needs. Send photographs, but allow for inspection before treating the old installation as suitable.

glazing.</a><a href="#glass">Etched glass: a finish built into the glazing choice.</a><a href="#privacy">Test privacy in the room, not just on a swatch.</a><a href="#branding">Use the glass as part of the interior design.</a><a href="#installation">Existing room or new fit-out: the project changes.</a><a href="#cost">Compare the complete scope of work.</a><a href="#scenarios">Examples of how the setting influences the decision.</a><a href="#decision">Keep decoration, privacy and safety as separate questions.</a><a href="#checklist">What to send us</a><a href="#faq">Questions & answers</a><a href="#sources">Sources & further reading</a><a href="#services">Explore the services</a></nav></aside><article class="reading-body"><section class="reading-section" id="start"><h2>Similar visual goals, different ways to achieve them.</h2><p>Frosted window film and etched glass can both soften a view through glazing while allowing a sense of light and openness. They are different products, however. Film is applied to a suitable glass surface. Etching changes the surface of the glass itself. That difference matters when you are adapting an existing office, specifying new partitions or planning how branding may change later.</p><p>Begin by defining the actual problem. Do you need to reduce a direct view into a treatment room, add a company logo to a meeting room or make a glazed door more noticeable? These are related but distinct requirements. A decorative pattern can look attractive without providing the level of privacy needed, and an opaque-looking sample can behave differently when someone stands close to the glass.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="at-a-glance"><h2>Compare at a glance.</h2><p class="table-hint">On a smaller screen, scroll across to compare all options.</p><div aria-label="Frosted window film vs etched glass comparison table" class="comparison-scroll" role="region" tabindex="0"><table><caption>Frosted window film vs etched glass at a glance</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Factor</th><th scope="col">Frosted window film</th><th scope="col">Etched glass</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">How it is made</th><td>Applied decorative layer</td><td>Treatment of the glass surface</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Existing glazing</th><td>May be applied if glass is suitable</td><td>Often a glazing replacement discussion</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Future branding</th><td>Can be considered for replacement graphics</td><td>Permanent finish is less adaptable</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Patterns and logos</th><td>Flexible applied graphic options</td><td>Discuss with specialist glass supplier</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Privacy</th><td>Depends on product, coverage and conditions</td><td>Also depends on finish and conditions</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Large areas</th><td>Discuss sheet width and visible joins</td><td>Discuss pane sizes and glazing joints</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Installation</th><td>Preparation and application to glass</td><td>Glass fabrication and fitting process</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Care</th><td>Follow film-specific cleaning guidance</td><td>Follow glass-treatment care guidance</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Best starting point</th><td>Adaptable branding in an existing space</td><td>Lasting finish within a new glazing scheme</td></tr></tbody></table></div></section><section class="reading-section" id="film"><h2>Frosted film: adaptable decoration for suitable existing glazing.</h2><p>Decorative film can create a frosted or etched-style appearance without replacing the pane solely to achieve that effect. <a href="https://www.3m.co.uk/3M/en_GB/p/d/b5005018057/">3M FASARA glass finishes</a> include patterned options designed to reproduce aspects of textured or etched glass appearance. The product range illustrates the design possibilities; the exact film and application should be chosen for your glazing.</p><p>Film is particularly worth discussing in an occupied office, a leased shop or a room where names and branding may change. Logos, bands and patterns can be incorporated into a considered layout. The ability to alter an applied graphic can be useful, although removal and replacement still require time, suitable methods and attention to the underlying surface.</p><p>The limitations include the suitability and condition of the glass, visible joins on large areas, exposed edges and the care needed during cleaning. Film should not be promised to conceal every scratch or defect. Some glazing has coatings or other characteristics that affect compatibility. Tell us what you know about the glass and arrange a check where the specification is uncertain.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="glass"><h2>Etched glass: a finish built into the glazing choice.</h2><p>Etched glass has a treated surface rather than an applied decorative layer. Acid-etched products are one example; <a href="https://www.pilkington.com/en/us/products/product-categories/decoration/pilkington-optifloat-opal">Pilkington Optifloat Opal</a> illustrates a manufactured decorative glass option. The exact glass construction, processing and installation should be specified by the glazing supplier for the intended application.</p><p>This route can suit a new fit-out where the glazing itself is being selected and a lasting decorative finish is wanted. It avoids relying on an applied film edge for the visual effect. That can be appealing in an architectural scheme where the glass is part of the permanent material palette and future graphic changes are unlikely.</p><p>The trade-off is reduced flexibility when the appearance or branding needs to change. Altering the treated finish is not equivalent to replacing a vinyl graphic. If new panes are required, the project involves glazing measurements, fabrication and installation rather than only a signage visit. Discuss the entire construction and any safety requirements with the glazing specialist.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="privacy"><h2>Test privacy in the room, not just on a swatch.</h2><p>Privacy is not a simple yes-or-no property shared by every frosted finish. The pattern, coverage, light on either side and the distance of people or objects from the glass affect what can be perceived. A narrow decorative band may interrupt a direct sightline while leaving views above and below it. That may be suitable for a meeting room but insufficient for a more private activity.</p><p>For a useful assessment, identify the positions that matter: seated at a desk, standing at a reception counter or passing through a corridor. Consider screens, paperwork and people as separate things to protect from view. Ask to review a sample under representative conditions, including evening lighting if the room is used after dark.</p><p>If genuine visual confidentiality is essential, say so explicitly and be prepared to consider a different coverage or room arrangement. Neither a fashionable pattern nor a general product name should be accepted as proof that sensitive information cannot be seen. A practical test with the proposed layout is more useful than relying on a photograph from another building.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="branding"><h2>Use the glass as part of the interior design.</h2><p>Film can carry repeated motifs, a restrained logo or a pattern coordinated with the surrounding brand. Think about the view from both sides. Text that reads correctly from the corridor may appear reversed from within the room, so decide which direction is primary and whether a non-text pattern would work better.</p><p>Align bands across adjacent panes and doors on the actual site layout. Door frames, handles and changes in floor level can interrupt a design that looks perfectly continuous in a flat artwork file. Record which panes open, which are fixed and where people naturally look through. A clear pane schedule helps prevent a repeated design from being applied to the wrong location.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="installation"><h2>Existing room or new fit-out: the project changes.</h2><p>For film on existing glazing, access, surface preparation and the condition of the pane are important. Furniture, blinds and fittings can affect access to the full surface. Share photographs before arranging the work, including edges and any existing graphics. If old film needs removal, include it in the quotation rather than treating it as a free preliminary task.</p><p>For new etched glazing, coordinate with the fit-out or glazing contractor before dimensions are finalised. The design, glass specification and installation sequence need to agree. A late request to change the decorative pattern can have wider implications than revising a printed proof. Keep responsibilities clear between the signage, glazing and building teams.</p><p>Ask for care instructions for the actual finished product. Cleaning staff should know which surface carries the film or treatment and which routine is recommended. Do not assume every cleaning chemical or abrasive tool is suitable.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="cost"><h2>Compare the complete scope of work.</h2><p>A film quotation and a replacement-glazing quotation may cover very different tasks. Compare design, preparation, old graphic removal, fitting and access in the film proposal. For etched glass, understand whether the price includes the glass supply, processing, transport, removal of old panes, installation and any associated making good.</p><p>If glazing is already being replaced, compare the additional cost of a decorative finish. If the room may change tenant or function, include the future alteration plan. Choose a solution that fits both the current project and the likely next change.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="scenarios"><h2>Examples of how the setting influences the decision.</h2><p>Illustrative example: a growing business leases an office with clear meeting-room partitions. Frosted film may provide a useful route to a branded band and a more private seated sightline without selecting new glazing solely for decoration. The proposal should test coverage around doors and review privacy from the corridor.</p><p>Illustrative example: an owner is commissioning a new interior with a long-term architectural palette. Etched glass may be worth considering alongside other glazing options because the panes are already part of the fit-out specification. The glazing contractor should confirm the appropriate construction and installation requirements.</p><p>Illustrative example: a treatment business wants to conceal activity behind a glazed partition. Start with the required privacy and representative lighting, rather than choosing a logo pattern first. A higher coverage, a different finish or a different partition solution may be needed. The decision should follow a practical assessment of the room.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="decision"><h2>Keep decoration, privacy and safety as separate questions.</h2><p>An attractive frosted effect does not by itself establish that a glazing installation meets every safety or accessibility requirement. If the project includes formal requirements for glass visibility, safety glazing or building compliance, obtain a project-specific specification from the responsible designer or specialist. Tell us those requirements at the outset so the decorative proposal can be coordinated with them.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="checklist"><h2>Your project checklist.</h2><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Photographs and approximate dimensions of every pane and door.</li><li>Whether the glazing is existing or part of a new fit-out.</li><li>The specific sightlines, people or information that need privacy.</li><li>Daylight and evening use, with lighting on each side of the glass.</li><li>Required logos, bands or patterns and the main viewing direction.</li><li>Known glass type, coatings, existing film and access restrictions.</li><li>Landlord approval, project specifications and any likely future changes.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">TALK THROUGH YOUR PROJECT ↗</a></p></section><section class="reading-section" id="faq"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Will frosted film make the room completely private?</summary><p>Not necessarily. Coverage, pattern, lighting and proximity to the glass matter. Explain the level of privacy required and review a sample under representative conditions before approving the layout.</p></details><details><summary>Can film be removed when we leave?</summary><p>Removal is often part of a planned film lifecycle, but the method, surface condition and lease requirements need checking. Do not assume it will be instant or cost-free. Agree the expectations with the landlord and installer.</p></details><details><summary>Does film replace safety glass?</summary><p>Ordinary decorative frosting should not be treated as a substitute for a required safety-glazing specification. Specialist films and glazing systems have different purposes. Have the responsible specialist confirm what the project requires.</p></details><details><summary>Can we add a logo to an existing frosted scheme?</summary><p>Possibly. Send photographs and details of the existing finish. Matching an older pattern, colour or level of opacity may need a sample, and the best solution may involve replacing a defined area rather than adding an unmatched patch.</p></details></section><section class="reading-section" id="sources"><h2>Sources & further reading.</h2><p class="source-note">Sources checked for this draft on 18 October 2026. Product ratings apply to the stated product and test conditions; confirm the current specification for your order.</p><ul class="source-links"><li><a class="" href="https://www.3m.co.uk/3M/en_GB/p/d/b5005018057/">3M FASARA decorative glass finishes ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.pilkington.com/en/us/products/product-categories/decoration/pilkington-optifloat-opal">Pilkington Optifloat Opal ↗</a></li></ul></section><section class="reading-section" id="services"><h2>Put the advice into practice.</h2><p>Tell us where the sign will go, what it needs to communicate and the date you are working towards. Our Norwich team can discuss the design, materials and fitting around your project.</p><div class="service-links"><a class="button" href="/signage-home/window-graphics">Frosted manifestation ↗</a><a mainEntity.name: Will frosted film make the room completely private?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Coverage, pattern, lighting and proximity to the glass matter. Explain the level of privacy required and review a sample under representative conditions before approving the layout.

mainEntity.name: Can film be removed when we leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removal is often part of a planned film lifecycle, but the method, surface condition and lease requirements need checking. Do not assume it will be instant or cost-free. Agree the expectations with the landlord and installer.

mainEntity.name: Does film replace safety glass?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ordinary decorative frosting should not be treated as a substitute for a required safety-glazing specification. Specialist films and glazing systems have different purposes. Have the responsible specialist confirm what the project requires.

mainEntity.name: Can we add a logo to an existing frosted scheme?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly. Send photographs and details of the existing finish. Matching an older pattern, colour or level of opacity may need a sample, and the best solution may involve replacing a defined area rather than adding an unmatched patch.
