href="#site-first">Start with the site, not a material name.</a><a href="#brief">Describe the signs your site needs.</a><a href="#panels">Consider a named exterior panel specification.</a><a href="#fixings">Treat fixings and supports as part of the sign.</a><a href="#wind">Do not assume a material choice solves wind exposure.</a><a href="#graphics">Match the graphics to the exposure and refresh cycle.</a><a href="#care">Make maintenance realistic for the premises.</a><a href="#examples">Three useful ways to plan a coastal signage project.</a><a href="#quote">Ask for a quote that explains the choices.</a><a href="#checklist">What to send us</a><a href="#faq">Questions & answers</a><a href="#sources">Sources & further reading</a><a href="#services">Explore the services</a></nav></aside><article class="reading-body"><section class="reading-section" id="site-first"><h2>Start with the site, not a material name.</h2><p>A coastal postcode is a useful warning to look more closely at the installation, but it is not a specification in itself. A shopfront set back on a sheltered street, an open holiday park entrance and a harbour-side building present different situations. Tell us exactly where the sign will go, how it will be supported and whether it needs to stay outdoors throughout the year.</p><p>For Norfolk and Suffolk businesses, photographs often explain the setting more clearly than a long description. Include a view towards the surrounding street or open area as well as a close image of the proposed position. Say if the sign is close to the sea, exposed above neighbouring buildings or frequently affected by blowing sand, spray or severe weather. These observations help guide the survey and product discussion.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="brief"><h2>Describe the signs your site needs.</h2><p>An entrance sign needs to identify the business before a visitor passes the turning. A reception panel welcomes someone already on the premises. A seasonal promotion needs a clear short-term message. List these jobs separately rather than asking every panel to carry the same amount of information. The intended viewing position and the information hierarchy should be agreed alongside the material choice.</p><p>Tell us which elements are permanent and which change. On a holiday park, the business name may remain stable while offers, opening hours or facilities change. On a coastal retail frontage, the fascia may be permanent while window promotions are renewed regularly. Separating those functions makes it easier to quote the appropriate product for each part and to plan updates without replacing an entire installation.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="panels"><h2>Consider a named exterior panel specification.</h2><p>Aluminium composite is one option to discuss for a rigid exterior sign, but products sold under that description are not all interchangeable. Ask for the actual manufacturer, grade, finish and thickness proposed. <a href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/details/dibond-registered-brand-solid-colours-1075/">3A Composites describes DIBOND Solid Colours as suitable for interior and exterior applications and identifies corrosion-resistant aluminium cover sheets</a>. Those product characteristics do not establish the suitability of every sign assembly for every coastal site.</p><p>Acrylic lettering, metal elements or a framed panel may be considered where the appearance calls for them. Rather than selecting a material because it sounds more premium, review a sample alongside the intended design and the installation details. A finish that looks attractive on a small sample still needs to work at the proposed size, viewing distance and mounting position.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="fixings"><h2>Treat fixings and supports as part of the sign.</h2><p>A durable face is only one part of an exterior installation. Ask the supplier to assess the support, fixing arrangement and compatibility of the components for the site. This is especially important when replacing a sign on an existing framework. A previous installation remaining in place is not evidence that the same supports will suit a different panel size, weight or shape.</p><p>Do not specify fixing quantities or substitute hardware from a generic shopping list. The installation needs to be assessed as a whole, including the substrate behind the sign. Let us know about a landlord’s requirements, an existing maintenance report or previous damage. These details can identify questions that should be resolved before manufacture, rather than leaving the fitting team to discover them on arrival.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="wind"><h2>Do not assume a material choice solves wind exposure.</h2><p>For an exposed position, the size, shape, support and mounting arrangement all deserve attention. A large panel on posts, a projecting sign and a face fixed against a building are different proposals. The person specifying the installation should establish what design assessment is necessary. This guide does not provide wind-load calculations or a universal fixing pattern for coastal signage.</p><p>The same principle applies to banners and portable signs. Choosing mesh instead of solid banner material does not prove that a fence, frame or fixing arrangement is adequate. A portable display should be used within its particular product instructions and operating limits. Tell us if the display needs to be brought indoors, stored between events or moved by one member of staff, so practicality is considered from the outset.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="graphics"><h2>Match the graphics to the exposure and refresh cycle.</h2><p>Choose the graphic system with the panel, rather than treating printing as an unrelated final step. Ask which vinyl or print finish is proposed and whether it is intended for the site conditions. <a href="https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0916/9158/1769/files/Reference_material_-_Metamark_Durability_Guide.pdf?v=1755610044">Metamark’s durability guidance</a> shows why exposure and installation conditions matter when interpreting a headline material rating. A number of years quoted for a raw film is not a coastal-life guarantee for a finished sign.</p><p>For a seasonal business, consider whether graphics should be renewed independently of the main support. Keeping dates, prices and special offers out of the permanent identity panel may simplify future changes. Ask about replacing a single panel if it is damaged and keep the approved artwork together with the material details. That makes a matching replacement easier to discuss later.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="care"><h2>Make maintenance realistic for the premises.</h2><p>Before choosing a complex installation, think about who will maintain it and how it will be reached. A sign that requires specialist access for every inspection or refresh has different practical implications from one reachable from ground level. Ask for aftercare instructions for the actual materials supplied and discuss whether a planned inspection arrangement is appropriate for the site.</p><p>Keep a simple record of the installation date, photographs and any concerns noticed during ordinary premises checks. If a panel moves unexpectedly, a fixing appears damaged or a part has come loose, arrange an assessment. Do not try to solve an installation issue by covering it with new vinyl or adding improvised fixings. Cosmetic refresh work and structural maintenance are separate decisions.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="examples"><h2>Three useful ways to plan a coastal signage project.</h2><p>For an illustrative seafront café, begin with a permanent business identity, a clearly located entrance message and separate menus that can be updated. Discuss the fascia as a surveyed installation, then look at how the operational information will change. This keeps the design focused and helps distinguish the cost of the enduring frontage from the cost of regular promotional updates.</p><p>For an illustrative holiday park, map the visitor journey from the road to reception and onward to the relevant facilities. Use that plan to identify the required signs before selecting materials. For a harbour-side workshop, start with the building identification, customer entrance and delivery instructions. These examples are planning approaches, not records of completed Broadland projects or specifications ready for manufacture.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="quote"><h2>Ask for a quote that explains the choices.</h2><p>A useful quotation should identify what is being supplied, why the proposed system suits the brief and what still depends on survey. Include the panel or lettering specification, graphics, installation scope and any access requirements. Ask how the sign could be refreshed or repaired later. Where there are alternative options, compare them against the same intended use rather than looking only at the total.</p><p>Send Broadland Digital the address, approximate dimensions, photographs and a short description of the business. Add the planned installation date and any times when the site is difficult to access. We can use that information to discuss a suitable starting point and identify which details need confirmation before a final specification is agreed.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="checklist"><h2>Your project checklist.</h2><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Photograph the sign position and the wider surroundings.</li><li>Describe direct exposure, shelter and seasonal use.</li><li>Separate permanent branding from changing information.</li><li>Request a named panel, graphics and fixing specification.</li><li>Have existing supports and the mounting surface assessed.</li><li>Agree aftercare, inspection and future replacement access.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">TALK THROUGH YOUR PROJECT ↗</a></p></section><section class="reading-section" id="faq"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Is aluminium composite automatically suitable by the sea?</summary><p>No material name establishes suitability on its own. The actual product, finish, graphics, supports and installation need to be assessed for the site. Ask for the proposed specification and any relevant limitations.</p></details><details><summary>Does mesh make a coastal banner safe in strong winds?</summary><p>Mesh is not a substitute for assessing the support and fixing arrangement. The complete installation and the supplier’s product limits must be considered; a generic banner recommendation cannot determine safe use at a particular site.</p></details><details><summary>Can I reuse the posts from an old sign?</summary><p>That needs an assessment of the existing posts, foundations and fixings against the new proposal. Supply photographs and any available installation records, but do not assume that previous use proves suitability.</p></details><details><summary>Should seasonal signs be stored indoors?</summary><p>Discuss storage and operation for the particular product. If it is designed to be taken down, keep its instructions and packaging and agree a practical routine with the staff who will handle it.</p></details></section><section class="reading-section" id="sources"><h2>Sources & further reading.</h2><p class="source-note">Sources checked for this draft on 18 October 2026. Product ratings apply to the stated product and test conditions; confirm the current specification for your order.</p><ul class="source-links"><li><a class="" href="https://www.display.3acomposites.com/en/products/details/dibond-registered-brand-solid-colours-1075/">3A Composites DIBOND Solid Colours product information ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0916/9158/1769/files/Reference_material_-_Metamark_Durability_Guide.pdf?v=1755610044">Metamark durability guide ↗</a></li></ul></section><section class="reading-section" id="services"><h2>Put the advice into practice.</h2><p>Tell us where the sign will go, what it needs to communicate and the date you are working towards. Our Norwich team can discuss the design, materials and fitting around your project.</p><div class="service-links"><a class="button" href="/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs">Shop and building signs ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/large-format-print/aluminium-composite-panels">Aluminium composite panels ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/large-format-print/mesh-banners">Mesh banners ↗</a></div><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Visit our Norwich workshop ↗</a> · <a class="" href="/sectors">Find signage for your sector ↗</a></p></section></article></div><section class="section tint"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid research-cards"><article class="card" data-search="How long do outdoor signs last? An outdoor sign is a combination of panel, graphics, fixings and installation. Here is how to choose a sensible specification, understand durability figures and plan for maintenance or a future refresh."><a href="/signage-home/guides-and-advice/how-long-do-outdoor-signs-last"><img alt="How long do outdoor signs last? — signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/how-long-do-outdoor-signs-last.webp" width="1600"/><h3>How long do outdoor signs last? ↗</h3></a><p>An outdoor sign is a combination of panel, graphics, fixings and installation. Here is how to choose a sensible specification, understand durability figures and plan for maintenance or a future refresh.</p></article><article class="card" data-search="PVC vs mesh banners A solid banner gives you a continuous print surface. mainEntity.name: Is aluminium composite automatically suitable by the sea?

mainEntity.name: Does mesh make a coastal banner safe in strong winds?

mainEntity.name: Can I reuse the posts from an old sign?

acceptedAnswer.text: That needs an assessment of the existing posts, foundations and fixings against the new proposal. Supply photographs and any available installation records, but do not assume that previous use proves suitability.

mainEntity.name: Should seasonal signs be stored indoors?

class="reading-section" id="assessment"><h2>Begin with the risk assessment, not a sign bundle.</h2><p>There is no single shopping list that makes every workplace safe. The signs for a warehouse, café, school and repair workshop follow the activities and risks at each site. <a href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/books/l64.htm">HSE guidance on safety signs and signals</a> explains that signs are needed where significant risks remain after other relevant measures have been taken. A warning board does not replace controlling the hazard. The legal framework is the <a href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1996/341/contents">Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations 1996, as amended</a>.</p><p>Ask the person responsible for workplace safety for the current assessment and any agreed action plan. Turn each signage action into a clear entry: what needs communicating, who needs to see it and where the decision is made. This gives the sign supplier something concrete to produce and prevents a generic pack from becoming a substitute for a considered site arrangement.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="messages"><h2>Understand the different message families.</h2><p><a href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/workplacetransport/safetysigns/">HSE’s safety-sign examples</a> distinguish prohibition, warning and mandatory signs. In broad terms, red circular prohibition signs restrict behaviour, yellow triangular warnings identify hazards and blue circular mandatory signs specify actions. These conventions are functional: choosing your brand colour instead can change how a message is understood.</p><p>Emergency escape and first-aid signs use green, while firefighting equipment identification uses red. The detailed <a href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/l64.pdf">HSE L64 guidance</a> explains these families and their use. Keep the recognised symbol at the centre of the message, with suitable supporting wording where needed. A decorative recreation should not be approved simply because its wording sounds correct.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="schedule"><h2>Build a location-based sign schedule.</h2><p>Create a spreadsheet or marked-up floor plan with a unique reference for every sign. Include the message, quantity, proposed position, viewing direction and material requirements. Add a photograph showing the intended fixing surface. The same instruction may be needed at more than one entrance to a controlled area, while several different notices may compete for attention at a single doorway.</p><p>Use practical location names such as loading-bay pedestrian entrance or first-floor east corridor. Avoid vague entries such as workshop sign, especially where more than one person will install or check the work. A clear schedule helps the responsible manager approve the arrangement, the supplier price it and the fitter place the right item in the right location.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="fire"><h2>Coordinate fire signs with the fire assessment.</h2><p>Fire safety has its own assessment and responsibilities. <a href="https://www.gov.uk/workplace-fire-safety-your-responsibilities/fire-risk-assessments">Government fire-risk-assessment guidance</a> explains that the responsible person must assess and review the premises, keep a written record and consider matters including escape routes, equipment, information and training. Use the resulting fire-sign requirements when preparing the order; a general sign catalogue cannot determine the escape strategy.</p><p>Keep escape-route references separate from ordinary visitor wayfinding on the plan. A sign directing someone to reception serves a different purpose from one identifying an escape route. Ask the responsible person or competent fire adviser to approve messages, arrows and locations before manufacture. If walls, doors or equipment have moved, update the plan first rather than automatically reproducing the previous set.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="viewing"><h2>Check where people will actually read the signs.</h2><p>Stand at each approach and note the distance and angle from which the message first needs to be understood. Include visitors arriving for the first time, delivery drivers and people entering from secondary doors. Record obstructions such as open doors, shelving, parked vehicles or stored materials. A photograph taken from directly in front of the fixing position does not show all these conditions.</p><p>HSE’s <a href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/l64.pdf">L64 guidance on signboards</a> calls for clear signs suited to viewing distance, adequate illumination, durable construction and secure fixing. It also warns against confusing clusters of signs. Use that information to discuss size and location with the responsible person. Enlarging a board may be less useful than moving it to the point where someone chooses a route.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="materials"><h2>Match the construction to the environment.</h2><p>Tell the supplier whether the sign is indoors, exposed to weather, regularly washed down or likely to be knocked by equipment. Include information about the surface: painted wall, glass, metal cladding, mesh fence or uneven masonry. Material and fixing choices should follow these conditions. A self-adhesive label and a rigid board can carry the same artwork while requiring very different installation preparation.</p><p>For cleaning areas, provide the cleaning method and any products that may contact the sign. For external locations, explain exposure and accessibility for maintenance. If a specialist performance specification applies, supply it rather than relying on a generic description such as heavy duty. Ask the quotation to identify the proposed construction so replacements can be ordered consistently.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="traffic"><h2>Include deliveries and changing work areas.</h2><p>Map the visitor route, vehicle entrance and delivery handover point as separate journeys. A new driver may need an instruction before entering a yard, while a pedestrian needs information before crossing into a working area. Share the site traffic plan with the person specifying signs. This helps avoid placing a warning after the point at which the intended decision should already have been made.</p><p>Temporary work needs an equally clear owner. Record who puts temporary notices out, who checks their position and who removes them when the activity ends. For example, a maintenance project may temporarily change access to a corridor. Its signage should be considered as part of that managed arrangement, rather than leaving an old arrow in place and hoping everyone remembers the verbal instruction.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="example"><h2>Example: refreshing signs in a mixed workshop.</h2><p>Imagine a workshop with a customer reception, vehicle working area and small parts store. The manager reviews the assessment and identifies a need to clarify customer access, equipment-related instructions and first-aid information. A numbered plan records the approved messages. Photographs show that one proposed position would be hidden whenever a roller door is open, so the placement is reconsidered before ordering.</p><p>The supplier then quotes the agreed signs by size, material and quantity. The manager checks the proof against the schedule, and the installer records the completed locations. This is an illustrative ordering workflow, not a prescribed safety scheme for every workshop. Its strength is that the assessment determines the requirement and the production process preserves that decision accurately.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="proof"><h2>Approve content and installation separately.</h2><p>A good proof approval checks spelling, symbols, arrows, sizes and references. Ask someone familiar with the site to check the content, particularly where similar messages appear in several areas. Avoid approving artwork from a small phone screenshot if the details cannot be read. Record approval against a revision number so an older file cannot accidentally become the production version.</p><p>After fitting, walk the site with the approved schedule. Confirm each reference is present and faces the intended approach. Check that nearby notices have not been left pointing elsewhere, and photograph the completed installation. Give the record to the person managing the premises. A tidy handover makes it easier to identify a missing sign during later changes or repairs.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="review"><h2>Maintain the information as the workplace changes.</h2><p>Give the sign schedule an owner and include it in the premises review process. New equipment, altered storage, changed access and relocated first-aid points can make old information unhelpful. Ask staff which notices are hard to see or regularly obscured. Their observations can reveal practical problems that were not apparent during an empty-building survey.</p><p>When replacing a damaged sign, check the message is still needed before copying it. Keep the artwork and material reference, but treat the replacement request as an opportunity to confirm the location. Good maintenance is partly physical and partly informational: a pristine board with an outdated instruction still needs attention.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="next"><h2>Send an approved schedule for a practical quotation.</h2><p>Broadland Digital can discuss the production and fitting of the signs identified for your premises. Send the approved schedule, photographs, quantities, sizes and any material or performance requirements. Explain whether the work is a full installation, a phased update or a small replacement order, and tell us how access to the work areas will be managed.</p><p>Start with safety and warning signs for workplace messages, fire and emergency signs for the approved fire-sign schedule, or site and safety signs for a wider project. The sign-making brief supports your workplace arrangements; it does not certify the risk assessment or replace competent advice about which controls and signs the premises need.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="checklist"><h2>Your project checklist.</h2><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Use the current workplace assessment and fire assessment.</li><li>Assign a unique reference and location to every required sign.</li><li>Get symbols, messages, arrows and positions approved.</li><li>Record viewing conditions, surfaces and environmental exposure.</li><li>Approve the final proof against the sign schedule.</li><li>Inspect the completed installation and assign responsibility for updates.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">TALK THROUGH YOUR PROJECT ↗</a></p></section><section class="reading-section" id="faq"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Is a standard safety-sign pack enough?</summary><p>Only if it happens to match the requirements identified for your premises. Use the assessment and site plan to establish the actual messages, quantities and locations.</p></details><details><summary>Can safety signs use our brand colours?</summary><p>Recognised safety colours and symbols have a specific purpose. Keep branding separate where it could confuse the safety message, and have the proposed design checked against the required specification.</p></details><details><summary>Who decides where fire-exit signs go?</summary><p>The arrangement should follow the premises fire assessment and advice of the responsible person or competent adviser. The sign supplier needs that approved schedule to manufacture and install the correct items.</p></details><details><summary>Can you replace a few damaged signs?</summary><p>Send clear photographs, measurements and any original references. Confirm with the responsible person that the messages and locations remain appropriate before reproducing them.</p></details></section><section class="reading-section" id="sources"><h2>Sources & further reading.</h2><p class="source-note">Sources checked for this draft on 18 October 2026. Product ratings apply to the stated product and test conditions; confirm the current specification for your order.</p><ul class="source-links"><li><a class="" href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/books/l64.htm">HSE: Safety signs and signals overview ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/l64.pdf">HSE L64: Guidance on the Safety Signs and Signals Regulations ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.hse.gov.uk/workplacetransport/safetysigns/">HSE: Safety-sign examples ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.gov.uk/workplace-fire-safety-your-responsibilities/fire-risk-assessments">GOV.UK: Fire risk assessments ↗</a></li><li><a class="" href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1996/341/contents">Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations 1996 ↗</a></li></ul><p class="source-note">This guide concerns England. The relevant authority or responsible project team should confirm the requirements for your premises. Technical production review is required before public launch.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="services"><h2>Put the advice into practice.</h2><p>Tell us where the sign will go, what it needs to communicate and the date you are working towards. Our Norwich team can discuss the design, materials and fitting around your project.</p><div class="service-links"><a class="button" href="/signage-home/site-safety-signs/safety-and-warning-signs">Safety and warning signs ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/site-safety-signs/fire-and-emergency-signs">Fire and emergency signs ↗</a><a class="button" href="/signage-home/site-safety-signs">Site and safety signs ↗</a></div><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Visit our Norwich workshop ↗</a> · <a class="" href="/sectors">Find signage for your sector ↗</a></p></section></article></div><section class="section tint"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid research-cards"><article class="card" data-search="Glass manifestation: what the regulations ask Plan visible glass markings for doors and screens, understand England’s building guidance and prepare a practical manifestation specification."><a href="/signage-home/guides-and-advice/glass-manifestation-regulations"><img alt="Glass manifestation: what the regulations ask — signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/glass-manifestation-regulations.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Glass manifestation: what the regulations ask ↗</h3></a><p>Plan visible glass markings for doors and screens, understand England’s building guidance and prepare a practical manifestation specification.</p></article><article class="card" data-search="How long do outdoor signs last? The banner and the structure carrying it still need to be suitable for the site.</p></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="options"><div class="wrap"><h2>Make it work for your project.</h2><div class="service-options"><article><span>01</span><h3>Perimeter and fence graphics for approved structures</h3></article><article><span>02</span><h3>Event and temporary promotional displays</h3></article><article><span>03</span><h3>Large-format graphics with planned joins and fixing positions</h3></article></div></div></section><section class="section" id="design"><div class="wrap"><h2>Considered design. Planned installation.</h2><div class="split"><div><h3>The right specification.</h3><p>Bold artwork works best when viewed across an open space. Leave generous spacing around lettering and use clear contrast. The mesh openings affect the printed appearance, so a dense photograph or fine text may not read like the same design on a solid material. We can discuss the viewing distance before settling the layout.</p></div><div><h3>Ready for the site.</h3><p>Provide the support dimensions and details of its condition, anchoring and exposure. Finishing and fixing arrangements should follow the actual installation. An exposed coastal position or elevated banner requires particular assessment; mesh alone is not evidence that a fence or scaffold is safe to carry advertising.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="checklist"><div class="wrap"><h2>Let’s get your project started.</h2><div class="split"><div><p>Send the details below to our Norwich team. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Is mesh windproof?</summary><p>No. It can allow airflow through the banner but still transfers load to the supporting structure. Suitability needs assessment for the installation.</p></details><details><summary>Will fine text reproduce clearly?</summary><p>Mesh is better suited to clear, bold messages. We review small text and image detail against the size and viewing distance.</p></details><details><summary>Can a mesh banner be reused?</summary><p>Reuse depends on its condition, storage and the new fixing arrangement. Inspect the material and finishing before putting it back into service.</p></details></div></section><section class="section tint" id="advice"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/guides-and-advice/sign-materials-for-coastal-sites"><img alt="Choosing sign materials for coastal sites signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/sign-materials-for-coastal-sites.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Choosing sign materials for coastal sites ↗</h3></a><p>Plan signage for a seafront shop, holiday park, harbour or coastal business by considering the complete installation: panel, graphics, fixings, exposure and future maintenance.</p></article><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/compare/pvc-vs-mesh-banners"><img alt="PVC vs mesh banners signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/pvc-vs-mesh-banners.webp" width="1600"/><h3>PVC vs mesh banners ↗</h3></a><p>A solid banner gives you a continuous print surface. <style>@import url('https://use.typekit.net/qbw1hzk.css');
.crmseo-d{--purple:#713fff;--ink:#2a2d32;--pale:#f5f1ff}
.crmseo-d *{box-sizing:border-box}
.crmseo-d{scroll-behavior:smooth;scroll-padding-top:80px}
.crmseo-d{margin:0;color:var(--ink);font-family:azo-sans-web,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:18px;line-height:1.65}
.crmseo-d h1,.crmseo-d h2,.crmseo-d h3,.crmseo-d h4{font-family:adelle,Georgia,serif;font-weight:800;line-height:1.15;letter-spacing:-.035em}
.crmseo-d h1{font-size:clamp(48px,5.8vw,86px);margin:24px 0}
.crmseo-d h2{font-size:clamp(34px,3.4vw,50px);color:var(--purple);margin:0 0 28px}
.crmseo-d h3{font-size:26px;margin:18px 0}
.crmseo-d p{margin:0 0 22px}
.crmseo-d a{color:inherit;text-underline-offset:5px}
.crmseo-d a:hover{opacity:.8}
.crmseo-d button,.crmseo-d input,.crmseo-d textarea,.crmseo-d select{font:inherit}
.crmseo-d button,.crmseo-d a,.crmseo-d input,.crmseo-d textarea,.crmseo-d summary{outline-offset:5px}
.crmseo-d .wrap{max-width:1366px;margin:auto;padding:0 64px}
.crmseo-d .review{background:#24262b;color:white;padding:12px 24px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:20px;font-size:13px}
.crmseo-d .review nav{display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.crmseo-d .review a{padding:7px 15px;text-decoration:none;border:1px solid #666;border-radius:20px}
.crmseo-d .review a.active{background:white;color:#25252a}
.crmseo-d .review label{white-space:nowrap}
.crmseo-d .brand{background:var(--purple);color:white}
.crmseo-d .header{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;padding-top:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #ffffff42}
.crmseo-d .logo{width:155px;height:58px;object-fit:contain}
.crmseo-d .nav{display:flex;gap:30px;align-items:center}
.crmseo-d .nav a{text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d .nav .selected{border-bottom:2px solid white}
.crmseo-d .button{display:inline-flex;padding:12px 26px;border:1px solid currentColor;border-radius:30px;text-decoration:none;font-size:14px;letter-spacing:.04em;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:18px;background:transparent;cursor:pointer}
.crmseo-d .button.white{background:white;color:var(--purple);border-color:white}
.crmseo-d .button.purple{background:var(--purple);color:white;border-color:var(--purple)}
.crmseo-d .hero{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.08fr 1fr;gap:55px;align-items:center;padding-top:65px;padding-bottom:80px}
.crmseo-d .eyebrow{text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.15em;font-size:12px;font-weight:700}
.crmseo-d .hero p{font-size:20px;max-width:580px}
.crmseo-d .actions{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:14px;margin-top:30px}
.crmseo-d .hero figure{margin:0}
.crmseo-d .hero img{width:100%;height:400px;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .hero figcaption{font-size:12px;margin-top:10px;color:#eee}
.crmseo-d .crumb{font-size:13px;padding-top:25px;padding-bottom:25px;color:#666}
.crmseo-d .jump{border-block:1px solid #ddd;background:white}
.crmseo-d .jump .wrap{display:flex;gap:28px;overflow:auto;padding-top:17px;padding-bottom:17px;white-space:nowrap;font-size:14px}
.crmseo-d .jump a{text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d .section{padding:90px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e5e5e5}

.crmseo-d .intro{max-width:790px}

.crmseo-d .grid.four{grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr)}

.crmseo-d .steps p{font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d details{border-bottom:1px solid #d8d2e1;padding:22px 0}
.crmseo-d summary{cursor:pointer;font-size:20px;font-weight:700}
.crmseo-d details p{margin:20px 0 0;font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d .tablewrap{overflow:auto}
.crmseo-d table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;min-width:670px;font-size:16px}

.crmseo-d thead th{background:var(--purple);color:white}
.crmseo-d tbody th{background:var(--pale)}
.crmseo-d td{color:#6c6475}

.crmseo-d .contents a{display:block;padding:9px 0;font-size:15px;color:var(--purple)}
.crmseo-d .articlebody{max-width:790px}
.crmseo-d .articlebody section{padding-bottom:55px;margin-bottom:45px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd}
.crmseo-d .articlebody h2{font-size:38px}
.crmseo-d .quote{font-family:adelle,Georgia,serif;font-size:28px;color:var(--purple);border-left:3px solid var(--purple);padding-left:25px}
.crmseo-d .enquiry{background:var(--purple);color:white}
.crmseo-d .enquiry h2{color:white}
.crmseo-d .enquiry .note{background:#ffffff14;color:white}
.crmseo-d .fields{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:20px}
.crmseo-d .fields label{display:flex;flex-direction:column;font-size:14px;gap:7px}
.crmseo-d .fields input,.crmseo-d .fields textarea,.crmseo-d .fields select{width:100%;border:1px solid #d6c6ff;padding:13px 15px;border-radius:0;background:white;color:var(--ink);font-weight:400}
.crmseo-d .fields .wide{grid-column:1/-1}
.crmseo-d .fields textarea{min-height:110px}
.crmseo-d .consent{font-size:13px;display:block;margin:20px 0}
.crmseo-d footer{background:var(--ink);color:white;padding:65px 0;font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d footer h3{color:white}
.crmseo-d footer .bottom{border-top:1px solid #555;padding-top:25px;margin-top:45px;font-size:12px}
.crmseo-d .meta{font-size:13px;color:#766d80}
.crmseo-d .status{font-size:14px;padding:12px 0}
.crmseo-d .inline-link{color:var(--purple)}
@media(max-width:900px){.crmseo-d .wrap{padding-left:28px;padding-right:28px}

.crmseo-d .hero img{height:340px}

.crmseo-d .grid.four{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}

}
@media(max-width:650px){.crmseo-d .review{align-items:flex-start;flex-direction:column;gap:8px}

.crmseo-d .review nav{gap:5px}
.crmseo-d .review a{padding:5px 10px}
.crmseo-d .header{gap:15px}
.crmseo-d .nav a:not(.selected):not(.button){display:none}
.crmseo-d .nav .button{padding:8px 12px;font-size:11px}
.crmseo-d .logo{width:125px}

.crmseo-d .hero{padding-top:35px;padding-bottom:40px}

.crmseo-d .hero p{font-size:18px}
.crmseo-d .section{padding:55px 0}

.crmseo-d .facts{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .facts div{border-bottom:1px solid #ded6ef}
.crmseo-d .fields{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .fields .wide{grid-column:auto}
.crmseo-d .contents{position:static}
.crmseo-d .card img{height:240px}
.crmseo-d .jump .wrap{gap:20px}
.crmseo-d .wrap{padding-left:22px;padding-right:22px}
}

mainEntity.name: How far is the workshop from Cromer, and where do I park?

acceptedAnswer.text: The A140 is the main approach from the Cromer area towards north Norwich. Our workshop is at Vulcan Road North, near the airport side of the city. Use the map to plan the journey from your actual premises and check conditions before departure. Our workshop postcode is NR6 6AQ. Mileage and drive time depend on your starting point and traffic; use the directions link for the current journey. Call 01603 407786 to discuss parking or accessibility before your visit. Plan your journey ↗

mainEntity.name: Can I see materials before ordering signs for Cromer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask to view the shortlisted finishes for the permanent sign and any changeable hospitality displays. A Cromer business may need several types of sign, but they can share an identity. Explain the exposed position and cleaning expectations as well as the visual style you prefer.

mainEntity.name: Do you survey and fit signs in Cromer, and is there a charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Cromer property, fitting plans need to consider the sign position, weather exposure and guest access. We discuss mounting surfaces and existing brackets before production, with a survey where needed. Share the busiest customer periods and your intended opening date so installation can be arranged around the premises. We will set out the agreed survey, delivery and installation work in your quotation.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you make and fit a sign in Cromer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us when you need your Cromer signs ready and whether that date is for collection or fitting. We will discuss a production schedule around the design, materials and installation involved. Approved artwork and any required permissions need to be in place before manufacture; mentioning your opening or launch date at the first enquiry helps us plan the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need advertisement consent for a sign in Cromer?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the sign and the Cromer property. Check with the relevant local planning authority and your landlord before committing to manufacture, especially for illuminated signs or a protected building. Send us any written requirements with your brief so the design can take them into account. Read the planning consent guide ↗

mainEntity.name: Is a pop-up display the same as a pull-up banner?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A pop-up typically creates a broader backdrop on an expanding frame, while a pull-up graphic retracts into a base cassette.

mainEntity.name: Can we order graphics for our existing frame?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send the exact system details and photographs. Compatibility must be established before artwork is prepared.

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on the system and size. We discuss the assembly instructions and practical handling requirements before you order.

We will discuss the specification, artwork and completion date before preparing your quotation.</p><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Required quantity, intended use and frequency of travel</li><li>Logo, headline, contact details and suitable images</li><li>Event date, delivery details and any existing hardware information</li></ul></div><div><h3>From brief to finished display.</h3><ol><li>Share your requirements, photographs and intended date.</li><li>Agree the quoted items, material specification and delivery or fitting arrangements.</li><li>Check the artwork, wording and dimensions before approving production.</li><li>Arrange collection, delivery or installation as agreed.</li></ol><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">Discuss pull-up banners ↗</a></div></div></div></section><section class="section" id="faq"><div class="wrap"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>What is the difference between budget and premium?</summary><p>The hardware construction, stability, handling and replacement options may differ. Compare the specific models rather than relying on the label alone.</p></details><details><summary>Can it be used outside?</summary><p>Only use a stand outdoors if it is specified for that purpose and the conditions are suitable. Standard indoor pull-up banners are not an outdoor substitute.</p></details><details><summary>Can you design the banner?</summary><p>Yes, send your brand files, main message and required details. We develop a layout for approval before production.</p></details></div></section><section class="section tint" id="advice"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/guides-and-advice/exhibition-stand-checklist"><img alt="Exhibition stand checklist signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/exhibition-stand-checklist.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Exhibition stand checklist ↗</h3></a><p>Plan your display from the booked floor space to the return journey: messaging, artwork, hardware, delivery, assembly and a practical checklist for the people attending the show.</p></article><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/compare/budget-vs-premium-pull-up-banners"><img alt="Budget vs premium pull-up banners signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/budget-vs-premium-pull-up-banners.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Budget vs premium pull-up banners ↗</h3></a><p>Match the stand to how often it travels, who assembles it and how long the message needs to last. Compare the hardware, printed graphic and replacement options separately.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="section" id="related"><div class="wrap"><h2>Explore related signage.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/signage-exhibition-stands/modular-exhibition-stands"><img alt="Modular exhibition stand with purple printed panels and a branded counter at a trade show" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/services/modular-exhibition-stands-norwich.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Modular exhibition stands ↗</h3></a><p>Plan a coordinated exhibition space around your team, message and event calendar. Modular displays bring reusable components together in layouts suited to the stand footprint.</p></article><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/signage-exhibition-stands/pop-up-displays"><img alt="Curved pop-up display with purple wave graphics beside its carry case" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/services/pop-up-displays-norwich.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Pop-up displays ↗</h3></a><p>Create a clear focal point for exhibitions, presentations and networking events with a portable pop-up display and coordinated graphics.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="norwich"><div class="wrap"><h2>Talk to our Norwich team.</h2><div class="split"><p>Visit Broadland Digital at Vulcan House, Vulcan Road North, Norwich, NR6 6AQ. Arrange a conversation about your project, materials and artwork, or send your photographs by email to get started.</p><div><a class="button" href="tel:01603407786">Call 01603 407786 ↗</a> <a class="button" href="mailto:production@broadlanddigital.co.uk">Email the team ↗</a><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Plan your visit ↗</a></p></div></div></div></section></main><section class="section tint crm-enquiry" id="enquiry"><div class="wrap"><h2>Discuss a project.</h2><p>Tell us about your premises, the signs you need and the date you are working towards. mainEntity.name: How far is the workshop from Lowestoft, and where do I park?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan the drive from Lowestoft to our north Norwich workshop using the directions link below. It lets you compare the available routes from your part of Lowestoft and check current traffic. The destination is Vulcan House, Vulcan Road North, NR6 6AQ. Our workshop postcode is NR6 6AQ. Mileage and drive time depend on your starting point and traffic; use the directions link for the current journey. Call 01603 407786 to discuss parking or accessibility before your visit. Plan your journey ↗

mainEntity.name: Can I see materials before ordering signs for Lowestoft?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Lowestoft hospitality premises, compare finishes around the customer-facing identity. For an operational site, bring the approved sign list and intended mounting details instead. A sample visit helps connect those choices to the finished appearance of your premises.

mainEntity.name: Do you survey and fit signs in Lowestoft, and is there a charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: We discuss collection, delivery and on-site fitting for your Lowestoft project as part of the quotation. Give us the full Suffolk address and any induction or access requirements, particularly for operational premises. For hospitality sites, include guest routes and busy periods so the proposed work can be planned around customers. We will set out the agreed survey, delivery and installation work in your quotation.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you make and fit a sign in Lowestoft?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us when you need your Lowestoft signs ready and whether that date is for collection or fitting. We will discuss a production schedule around the design, materials and installation involved. Approved artwork and any required permissions need to be in place before manufacture; mentioning your opening or launch date at the first enquiry helps us plan the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need advertisement consent for a sign in Lowestoft?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the sign and the Lowestoft property. Check with the relevant local planning authority and your landlord before committing to manufacture, especially for illuminated signs or a protected building. Send us any written requirements with your brief so the design can take them into account. Read the planning consent guide ↗

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you make and fit a sign in Norfolk?

Approved artwork and any required permissions need to be in place before manufacture; mentioning your opening or launch date at the first enquiry helps us plan the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need advertisement consent for a sign in Norfolk?

Check with the relevant local planning authority and your landlord before committing to manufacture, especially for illuminated signs or a protected building. Send us any written requirements with your brief so the design can take them into account. Read the planning consent guide ↗

acceptedAnswer.text: If your North Walsham project includes both a shopfront and internal signs, ask to compare the finishes together. For a trade counter, show where customers wait and collect items. Samples are most useful when linked to an actual sign position and a clear communication task.

mainEntity.name: Do you survey and fit signs in North Walsham, and is there a charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us how customers and delivery drivers use your North Walsham premises. mainEntity.name: How quickly can you make and fit a sign in North Walsham?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us when you need your North Walsham signs ready and whether that date is for collection or fitting. We will discuss a production schedule around the design, materials and installation involved. Approved artwork and any required permissions need to be in place before manufacture; mentioning your opening or launch date at the first enquiry helps us plan the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need advertisement consent for a sign in North Walsham?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the sign and the North Walsham property. Check with the relevant local planning authority and your landlord before committing to manufacture, especially for illuminated signs or a protected building. Send us any written requirements with your brief so the design can take them into account. Read the planning consent guide ↗

mainEntity.name: How far is the workshop from Norwich, and where do I park?

acceptedAnswer.text: From the city, head towards the north Norwich ring road and Vulcan Road North. Our workshop is on the airport side of Norwich, so set your destination to Vulcan House rather than a city-centre address. Our workshop postcode is NR6 6AQ. Mileage and drive time depend on your starting point and traffic; use the directions link for the current journey. Call 01603 407786 to discuss parking or accessibility before your visit. Plan your journey ↗

mainEntity.name: Can I see materials before ordering signs for Norwich?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, request a material appointment around the options relevant to your frontage. A city shop might need to compare lettering against painted timber; an office might need to see a privacy finish. Send those photographs ahead so the samples answer a real design question.

mainEntity.name: Do you survey and fit signs in Norwich, and is there a charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: For city shops, we plan around pedestrian access and trading hours. For offices and commercial units, we look at the approach, fixing surface and any shared entrances. Send your Norwich postcode and photographs so we can discuss the survey, delivery and installation your project needs. We will set out the agreed survey, delivery and installation work in your quotation.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you make and fit a sign in Norwich?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us when you need your Norwich signs ready and whether that date is for collection or fitting. We will discuss a production schedule around the design, materials and installation involved. Approved artwork and any required permissions need to be in place before manufacture; mentioning your opening or launch date at the first enquiry helps us plan the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need advertisement consent for a sign in Norwich?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the sign and the Norwich property. Check with the relevant local planning authority and your landlord before committing to manufacture, especially for illuminated signs or a protected building. Send us any written requirements with your brief so the design can take them into account. Read the planning consent guide ↗

mainEntity.name: Can I see materials before ordering signs for Wymondham?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Wymondham refurbishment, compare samples against the intended decoration and building finishes. If the frontage and reception are being designed together, look at those choices as one family. Keep an approved reference so later room signs or privacy graphics can remain consistent.

mainEntity.name: Do you survey and fit signs in Wymondham, and is there a charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Wymondham refurbishment, we coordinate the sign brief with the readiness of the premises. Freshly prepared walls, new glazing and landlord approvals can all affect the fitting sequence. Share the fit-out dates and access contact so survey, manufacture and installation can be discussed around the actual programme. We will set out the agreed survey, delivery and installation work in your quotation.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you make and fit a sign in Wymondham?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us when you need your Wymondham signs ready and whether that date is for collection or fitting. We will discuss a production schedule around the design, materials and installation involved. Approved artwork and any required permissions need to be in place before manufacture; mentioning your opening or launch date at the first enquiry helps us plan the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need advertisement consent for a sign in Wymondham?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the sign and the Wymondham property. Check with the relevant local planning authority and your landlord before committing to manufacture, especially for illuminated signs or a protected building. Send us any written requirements with your brief so the design can take them into account. Read the planning consent guide ↗

We can produce the specified signage; the responsible person or appointed adviser should confirm the route, message, symbol and position before artwork approval.</p></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="options"><div class="wrap"><h2>Make it work for your project.</h2><div class="service-options"><article><span>01</span><h3>Escape-route and exit identification from an approved plan</h3></article><article><span>02</span><h3>Fire-equipment identification and action notices</h3></article><article><span>03</span><h3>Replacement or additional signs for an agreed building update</h3></article></div></div></section><section class="section" id="design"><div class="wrap"><h2>Considered design. Planned installation.</h2><div class="split"><div><h3>The right specification.</h3><p>Legibility, viewing distance, lighting and mounting position all influence the specification. Keep recognised safety symbols and colours intact. A brand treatment should not obscure the meaning of a safety sign. Confirm any requirements for illumination or photoluminescent material with the responsible project team.</p></div><div><h3>Ready for the site.</h3><p>Changing a room layout or escape route can affect more than one sign. Use a numbered schedule that ties every item to its location, and check arrows against the actual route. The completed installation should be reviewed by the responsible team; a new set of signs does not itself certify the premises.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="checklist"><div class="wrap"><h2>Let’s get your project started.</h2><div class="split"><div><p>Send the details below to our Norwich team. We will discuss the specification, artwork and completion date before preparing your quotation.</p><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Approved sign schedule and relevant plan</li><li>Required symbols, wording, sizes and material specification</li><li>Mounting locations, quantities and installation arrangements</li></ul></div><div><h3>From brief to finished display.</h3><ol><li>Share your requirements, photographs and intended date.</li><li>Agree the quoted items, material specification and delivery or fitting arrangements.</li><li>Check the artwork, wording and dimensions before approving production.</li><li>Arrange collection, delivery or installation as agreed.</li></ol><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">Discuss fire and emergency signs ↗</a></div></div></div></section><section class="section" id="faq"><div class="wrap"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Can you decide our escape routes?</summary><p>The building’s responsible person or competent adviser must establish the emergency arrangements. We work from the approved requirements.</p></details><details><summary>Do all emergency signs need to glow in the dark?</summary><p>Do not assume one material suits every position. The assessment and lighting arrangements determine the required specification.</p></details><details><summary>Can we replace individual damaged signs?</summary><p>Yes, provide the approved design, dimensions, material and location. Check that the existing message remains appropriate before matching it.</p></details></div></section><section class="section tint" id="advice"><div class="wrap"><h2>A little more guidance.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/guides-and-advice/workplace-safety-sign-requirements"><img alt="Safety signs your workplace needs signage example" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/research/workplace-safety-sign-requirements.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Safety signs your workplace needs ↗</h3></a><p>Build a useful safety-sign schedule from your risk assessment, then choose clear messages, suitable materials and practical installation positions.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="section" id="related"><div class="wrap"><h2>Explore related signage.</h2><div class="grid service-cards"><article class="card"><a href="/signage-home/site-safety-signs/safety-and-warning-signs"><img alt="General warning and hard hat safety signs at a workshop entrance" height="900" loading="lazy" src="https://dipjypzrfigkzuarlsov.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/seo-images/ae4393de-99e2-4a0f-be28-2866e44443bd/signage/services/safety-and-warning-signs-norwich.webp" width="1600"/><h3>Safety and warning signs ↗</h3></a><p>Workplace and site signs produced from your approved risk-assessment requirements, with clear symbols, readable wording and materials suited to the position.</p></article></div></div></section><section class="section tint" id="norwich"><div class="wrap"><h2>Talk to our Norwich team.</h2><div class="split"><p>Visit Broadland Digital at Vulcan House, Vulcan Road North, Norwich, NR6 6AQ. Arrange a conversation about your project, materials and artwork, or send your photographs by email to get started.</p><div><a class="button" href="tel:01603407786">Call 01603 407786 ↗</a> <a class="button" href="mailto:production@broadlanddigital.co.uk">Email the team ↗</a><p><a class="" href="/signage-home/signage-norwich">Plan your visit ↗</a></p></div></div></div></section></main><section class="section tint crm-enquiry" id="enquiry"><div class="wrap"><h2>Discuss a project.</h2><p>Tell us about your premises, the signs you need and the date you are working towards. .crmseo-d{scroll-behavior:smooth;scroll-padding-top:80px}
.crmseo-d{margin:0;color:var(--ink);font-family:azo-sans-web,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:18px;line-height:1.65}
.crmseo-d h1,.crmseo-d h2,.crmseo-d h3,.crmseo-d h4{font-family:adelle,Georgia,serif;font-weight:800;line-height:1.15;letter-spacing:-.035em}
.crmseo-d h1{font-size:clamp(48px,5.8vw,86px);margin:24px 0}
.crmseo-d h2{font-size:clamp(34px,3.4vw,50px);color:var(--purple);margin:0 0 28px}
.crmseo-d h3{font-size:26px;margin:18px 0}
.crmseo-d p{margin:0 0 22px}
.crmseo-d a{color:inherit;text-underline-offset:5px}
.crmseo-d a:hover{opacity:.8}
.crmseo-d button,.crmseo-d input,.crmseo-d textarea,.crmseo-d select{font:inherit}
.crmseo-d button,.crmseo-d a,.crmseo-d input,.crmseo-d textarea,.crmseo-d summary{outline-offset:5px}
.crmseo-d .wrap{max-width:1366px;margin:auto;padding:0 64px}
.crmseo-d .review{background:#24262b;color:white;padding:12px 24px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:20px;font-size:13px}
.crmseo-d .review nav{display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.crmseo-d .review a{padding:7px 15px;text-decoration:none;border:1px solid #666;border-radius:20px}
.crmseo-d .review a.active{background:white;color:#25252a}
.crmseo-d .review label{white-space:nowrap}
.crmseo-d .brand{background:var(--purple);color:white}
.crmseo-d .header{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;padding-top:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #ffffff42}
.crmseo-d .logo{width:155px;height:58px;object-fit:contain}
.crmseo-d .nav{display:flex;gap:30px;align-items:center}
.crmseo-d .nav a{text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d .nav .selected{border-bottom:2px solid white}
.crmseo-d .button{display:inline-flex;padding:12px 26px;border:1px solid currentColor;border-radius:30px;text-decoration:none;font-size:14px;letter-spacing:.04em;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:18px;background:transparent;cursor:pointer}
.crmseo-d .button.white{background:white;color:var(--purple);border-color:white}
.crmseo-d .button.purple{background:var(--purple);color:white;border-color:var(--purple)}
.crmseo-d .hero{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.08fr 1fr;gap:55px;align-items:center;padding-top:65px;padding-bottom:80px}
.crmseo-d .eyebrow{text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.15em;font-size:12px;font-weight:700}
.crmseo-d .hero p{font-size:20px;max-width:580px}
.crmseo-d .actions{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:14px;margin-top:30px}
.crmseo-d .hero figure{margin:0}
.crmseo-d .hero img{width:100%;height:400px;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .hero figcaption{font-size:12px;margin-top:10px;color:#eee}
.crmseo-d .crumb{font-size:13px;padding-top:25px;padding-bottom:25px;color:#666}
.crmseo-d .jump{border-block:1px solid #ddd;background:white}
.crmseo-d .jump .wrap{display:flex;gap:28px;overflow:auto;padding-top:17px;padding-bottom:17px;white-space:nowrap;font-size:14px}
.crmseo-d .jump a{text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d .section{padding:90px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e5e5e5}
.crmseo-d .tint{background:var(--pale)}
.crmseo-d .split{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:75px;align-items:start}
.crmseo-d .intro{max-width:790px}
.crmseo-d .note{font-size:13px;color:#61516e;border-left:3px solid #b79cff;padding:9px 14px;background:#f5f1ff;margin:18px 0;line-height:1.6}
.crmseo-d .brand .note{background:#ffffff13;border-color:#d6c8ff;color:white}
.crmseo-d .hide-notes .note{display:none}
.crmseo-d .slot{padding:24px;border:1px dashed #bcb4cb;min-height:120px;background:#faf9fc;color:#696371;font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d .slot strong{display:block;color:#514261;margin-bottom:8px}
.crmseo-d .facts{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);border:1px solid #ded6ef;margin-top:36px}
.crmseo-d .facts div{padding:26px;border-right:1px solid #ded6ef}
.crmseo-d .facts b{display:block;font-size:24px;color:var(--purple)}
.crmseo-d .grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);gap:32px}
.crmseo-d .grid.four{grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr)}
.crmseo-d .card{border-bottom:1px solid #d9d4df;padding-bottom:26px}
.crmseo-d .card img{height:220px;width:100%;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .card a{color:var(--purple);font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d .card p{font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d .image-slot{height:240px;background:#eee9f6;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:1px dashed #bfb4d4;color:#736581;text-align:center;padding:30px}
.crmseo-d .listlinks{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px}
.crmseo-d .listlinks a{padding:12px 19px;border:1px solid #d7c9f5;text-decoration:none;border-radius:26px;color:var(--purple);font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d .steps{counter-reset:step;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:30px}
.crmseo-d .steps article:before{counter-increment:step;content:'0' counter(step);font-family:adelle,Georgia,serif;font-size:42px;color:#a088d8}
.crmseo-d .steps p{font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d details{border-bottom:1px solid #d8d2e1;padding:22px 0}
.crmseo-d summary{cursor:pointer;font-size:20px;font-weight:700}
.crmseo-d details p{margin:20px 0 0;font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d .tablewrap{overflow:auto}
.crmseo-d table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;min-width:670px;font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d th,.crmseo-d td{text-align:left;padding:20px;border:1px solid #ddd4ed}
.crmseo-d thead th{background:var(--purple);color:white}
.crmseo-d tbody th{background:var(--pale)}
.crmseo-d td{color:#6c6475}
.crmseo-d .article{display:grid;grid-template-columns:240px 1fr;gap:70px}
.crmseo-d .contents{position:sticky;top:30px;border-top:3px solid var(--purple);padding-top:20px}
.crmseo-d .contents a{display:block;padding:9px 0;font-size:15px;color:var(--purple)}
.crmseo-d .articlebody{max-width:790px}
.crmseo-d .articlebody section{padding-bottom:55px;margin-bottom:45px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd}
.crmseo-d .articlebody h2{font-size:38px}
.crmseo-d .quote{font-family:adelle,Georgia,serif;font-size:28px;color:var(--purple);border-left:3px solid var(--purple);padding-left:25px}
.crmseo-d .enquiry{background:var(--purple);color:white}
.crmseo-d .enquiry h2{color:white}
.crmseo-d .enquiry .note{background:#ffffff14;color:white}
.crmseo-d .fields{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:20px}
.crmseo-d .fields label{display:flex;flex-direction:column;font-size:14px;gap:7px}
.crmseo-d .fields input,.crmseo-d .fields textarea,.crmseo-d .fields select{width:100%;border:1px solid #d6c6ff;padding:13px 15px;border-radius:0;background:white;color:var(--ink);font-weight:400}
.crmseo-d .fields .wide{grid-column:1/-1}
.crmseo-d .fields textarea{min-height:110px}
.crmseo-d .consent{font-size:13px;display:block;margin:20px 0}
.crmseo-d footer{background:var(--ink);color:white;padding:65px 0;font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d footer h3{color:white}
.crmseo-d footer .bottom{border-top:1px solid #555;padding-top:25px;margin-top:45px;font-size:12px}
.crmseo-d .meta{font-size:13px;color:#766d80}
.crmseo-d .status{font-size:14px;padding:12px 0}
.crmseo-d .inline-link{color:var(--purple)}
@media(max-width:900px){.crmseo-d .wrap{padding-left:28px;padding-right:28px}
.crmseo-d .hero{gap:30px}
.crmseo-d .hero img{height:340px}
.crmseo-d .nav{gap:15px;font-size:14px}
.crmseo-d .grid.four{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}
.crmseo-d .split{gap:35px}
.crmseo-d .article{grid-template-columns:180px 1fr;gap:30px}
}
@media(max-width:650px){.crmseo-d .review{align-items:flex-start;flex-direction:column;gap:8px}
.crmseo-d .review>strong{display:none}
.crmseo-d .review nav{gap:5px}
.crmseo-d .review a{padding:5px 10px}
.crmseo-d .header{gap:15px}
.crmseo-d .nav a:not(.selected):not(.button){display:none}
.crmseo-d .nav .button{padding:8px 12px;font-size:11px}
.crmseo-d .logo{width:125px}
.crmseo-d .hero,.crmseo-d .split,.crmseo-d .article{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .hero{padding-top:35px;padding-bottom:40px}
.crmseo-d .hero img{height:260px}
.crmseo-d .hero p{font-size:18px}
.crmseo-d .section{padding:55px 0}
.crmseo-d .grid,.crmseo-d .steps{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .grid.four{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:20px}
.crmseo-d .facts{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .facts div{border-bottom:1px solid #ded6ef}
.crmseo-d .fields{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .fields .wide{grid-column:auto}
.crmseo-d .contents{position:static}
.crmseo-d .card img{height:240px}
.crmseo-d .jump .wrap{gap:20px}
.crmseo-d .wrap{padding-left:22px;padding-right:22px}
}
.crmseo-d .guidance-image-link{display:block;overflow:hidden;margin-bottom:24px}
.crmseo-d .guidance-image{display:block;width:100%;height:auto!important;aspect-ratio:16/10;object-fit:cover;transition:transform .2s ease}
.crmseo-d .guidance-image-link:hover .guidance-image{transform:scale(1.025)}
.crmseo-d #advice .split{gap:32px}
.crmseo-d #advice article{border-bottom:1px solid #d9d4df;padding-bottom:28px}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.crmseo-d .guidance-image{transition:none}
}
.crmseo-d footer.live-footer{background:#713fff;color:#fff;padding:100px 0 40px;font-size:18px}
.crmseo-d footer.live-footer a{color:#fff;text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d footer.live-footer .wrap{padding-left:100px;padding-right:100px}
.crmseo-d .live-footer .footer-form h2{font-family:azo-sans-web,Arial,sans-serif;color:#fff;font-size:42px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:normal;margin:0 0 100px}
.crmseo-d .footer-inputs{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);gap:35px}
.crmseo-d .footer-inputs label{min-width:0}
.crmseo-d .live-footer input:not([type=checkbox]),.crmseo-d .live-footer textarea{display:block;width:100%;border:none;border-bottom:1px solid white;background:transparent;color:white;padding:16px 0;border-radius:0}
.crmseo-d .live-footer input::placeholder,.crmseo-d .live-footer textarea::placeholder{color:white;opacity:1}
.crmseo-d .live-footer textarea{height:42px;min-height:42px;margin:20px 0 40px;resize:vertical;padding:0}
.crmseo-d .footer-form-bottom{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:20px}
.crmseo-d .footer-form-bottom button{background:transparent;border:2px solid white;border-radius:24px;color:white;padding:7.5px 30px;cursor:pointer}
.crmseo-d .footer-contacts{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr auto;gap:48px;margin-top:150px}
.crmseo-d .live-footer .footer-contacts h3{font-size:23px;font-weight:700;color:white;letter-spacing:normal;margin:0 0 20px}
.crmseo-d .footer-contacts address{font-style:normal;margin-top:26px}
.crmseo-d .footer-contacts a{overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.crmseo-d .footer-news{display:block;margin-top:16px}
.crmseo-d .footer-legal{padding-top:24px;font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d .footer-preview{font-size:12px;opacity:.8;margin:15px 0 0}
.crmseo-d .footer-project-details{padding:0 0 22px;border:0;font-size:14px}
.crmseo-d .footer-project-details summary{font-size:14px;font-weight:400}
.crmseo-d .footer-project-details label{display:block;margin:18px 0}
.crmseo-d .sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0}
@media(max-width:900px){.crmseo-d footer.live-footer .wrap{padding-inline:28px}
.crmseo-d .footer-contacts{gap:25px;font-size:16px}
}
@media(max-width:650px){.crmseo-d footer.live-footer{padding-top:55px}
.crmseo-d .live-footer .footer-form h2{font-size:34px;margin-bottom:45px}
.crmseo-d .footer-inputs{grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:12px}
.crmseo-d .footer-contacts{grid-template-columns:1fr;margin-top:70px;gap:35px}
.crmseo-d .footer-contacts h3[aria-hidden]{display:none}
.crmseo-d .footer-form-bottom{align-items:flex-start}
.crmseo-d .footer-form-bottom label{font-size:14px}
.crmseo-d .footer-legal{font-size:12px}
}
.crmseo-d .approval{padding:9px 20px;text-align:center;background:#2a2d32;color:white;font-size:12px}
.crmseo-d .hero-title{padding:65px 0 55px}
.crmseo-d .hero-title h1{font-size:clamp(52px,7vw,100px);margin:12px 0 25px}
.crmseo-d .hero-title p{max-width:850px;font-size:23px}
.crmseo-d .hero-band{background:linear-gradient(to bottom,#713fff 65%,white 65%)}
.crmseo-d .big-hero{width:100%;aspect-ratio:16/9;object-fit:cover;display:block}
.crmseo-d .hero-caption{font-size:12px;color:#777;margin:12px 0 0}
.crmseo-d .picture{align-items:center}
.crmseo-d .picture>img{width:100%;height:520px;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .pending{font-size:13px;color:#786980;border-left:2px solid #bda9ee;padding-left:14px;margin-top:22px}
.crmseo-d .visit-panel{border:1px solid #d7caef;padding:35px;background:white}
.crmseo-d .visit-panel h3{color:#713fff}
.crmseo-d .visit-panel dl{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:16px;font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d .visit-panel dd{margin:0;color:#777}
.crmseo-d .map-slot{display:block;background:#f5f1ff;padding:35px;text-align:center;color:#756685}
.crmseo-d .villages{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:0;margin:35px 0 55px}
.crmseo-d .villages span{padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #d5c8e7;font-family:adelle,Georgia,serif;font-size:22px;color:#713fff}
.crmseo-d .review-space{max-width:850px}
.crmseo-d .review-space .quote{font-size:38px;margin-top:25px}
.crmseo-d .grid.four h3{font-size:25px}
.crmseo-d .grid.four .card img{height:240px}
.crmseo-d .nav .other{opacity:.8}
.crmseo-d .section{padding:100px 0}
.crmseo-d .note{display:none}
@media(max-width:650px){.crmseo-d .hero-title{padding:35px 0}
.crmseo-d .hero-title p{font-size:19px}
.crmseo-d .picture>img{height:310px}
.crmseo-d .villages{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr}
.crmseo-d .section{padding:55px 0}
.crmseo-d .visit-panel{padding:20px}
.crmseo-d .grid.four{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .big-hero{aspect-ratio:4/3}
.crmseo-d .review-space .quote{font-size:29px}
}
.crmseo-d .location-picker{display:flex;gap:15px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin:0 auto;padding-top:18px;padding-bottom:18px;border-bottom:1px solid #ddd}
.crmseo-d .location-picker label{font-size:13px;font-weight:700}
.crmseo-d .location-picker select{padding:8px 35px 8px 12px;background:white;border:1px solid #cabceb;color:#4d2d99;max-width:100%}
.crmseo-d .location-picker a{font-size:13px;color:#713fff}
.crmseo-d .block-photo{width:100%;height:auto;aspect-ratio:16/10;object-fit:cover;display:block}
.crmseo-d .picture figure{margin:0}
.crmseo-d .picture figure img{width:100%;height:auto;aspect-ratio:4/3;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .picture figcaption,.crmseo-d .image-caption{font-size:11px;color:#79717e;margin-top:8px;line-height:1.4}
.crmseo-d .steps img{width:100%;height:auto;aspect-ratio:4/3;object-fit:cover;margin-bottom:20px}
.crmseo-d .steps article:before{display:none}
.crmseo-d .steps .number{font:800 35px adelle,Georgia,serif;color:#a088d8}
.crmseo-d .local-article{column-count:2;column-gap:65px}
.crmseo-d .local-article p{break-inside:avoid}
.crmseo-d .sector-grid img{width:100%;aspect-ratio:16/10;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .location-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);gap:38px}
.crmseo-d .location-grid a{text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d .location-grid img{width:100%;height:auto;aspect-ratio:16/10;object-fit:cover}
.crmseo-d .location-grid h3{color:#713fff}
.crmseo-d .location-grid p{font-size:16px}
.crmseo-d .visit-panel{margin-top:20px}
.crmseo-d .picture .section-note{font-size:13px}
.crmseo-d .page-proof{margin-top:22px;color:#76677f;font-size:13px}
.crmseo-d .big-hero{height:auto;aspect-ratio:16/9}
.crmseo-d .guidance-image{aspect-ratio:16/10}
.crmseo-d .review-placeholder{padding:28px;border-left:3px solid #713fff;background:white}
.crmseo-d .location-nav-links{display:flex;gap:18px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.crmseo-d .location-nav-links a{color:#713fff}
.crmseo-d .pending{line-height:1.5}
.crmseo-d #areas .split{align-items:start}
.crmseo-d .facts b{font-size:clamp(18px,2.2vw,30px)}
.crmseo-d .facts a{color:inherit;text-decoration-thickness:1px;text-underline-offset:5px}
.crmseo-d .map-slot{font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d .workshop-map iframe{display:block;width:100%;height:320px;border:0}
@media(max-width:650px){.crmseo-d .nav a[href="/sectors/"]{display:inline-block;font-size:12px}
.crmseo-d .nav{gap:10px}
.crmseo-d .local-article{column-count:1}
.crmseo-d .location-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.crmseo-d .steps{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr}
.crmseo-d .steps h3{font-size:21px}
.crmseo-d .steps p{font-size:15px}
.crmseo-d .picture figure img{aspect-ratio:4/3}
.crmseo-d .big-hero{aspect-ratio:4/3}
}
.crmseo-d .sector-preview{background:#2a2d32;color:#fff;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.13em;text-align:center;padding:9px 20px}
.crmseo-d .sector-hero{padding-top:65px;padding-bottom:100px}
.crmseo-d .sector-hero h1{max-width:1100px;white-space:pre-line;font-size:clamp(42px,5.4vw,78px)}
.crmseo-d .sector-hero p{font-size:22px;max-width:850px}
.crmseo-d .sector-hero-image{margin-top:-50px;position:relative}
.crmseo-d .sector-hero-image img{width:100%;height:auto;aspect-ratio:16/7;object-fit:cover;display:block}
.crmseo-d .sector-groups{display:grid;gap:70px}
.crmseo-d .sector-panel{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:50px;align-items:center;border-bottom:1px solid #ded6ef;padding-bottom:65px}
.crmseo-d .sector-panel:nth-child(even) .sector-panel-image{order:2}
.crmseo-d .sector-panel img{width:100%;height:auto;aspect-ratio:4/3;object-fit:cover;display:block}
.crmseo-d .sector-panel h2{font-size:36px;margin:12px 0 22px}
.crmseo-d .sector-panel h2 a{text-decoration:none}
.crmseo-d .sector-panel-copy>p{font-size:17px}
.crmseo-d .sector-child-links{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:9px 18px;margin:22px 0 28px}
.crmseo-d .sector-child-links a{font-size:14px;color:var(--purple)}
.crmseo-d .directory-search{margin-bottom:55px;max-width:760px}
.crmseo-d .directory-search label{font-weight:700;display:block;margin-bottom:12px}
.crmseo-d .directory-search input{border:1px solid #aa90e2;width:100%;padding:17px 20px;background:white;color:var(--ink);border-radius:0}

Silhouettes and movement can remain visible depending on the film, lighting and distance from the glass. Reflective films behave differently and should not be treated as guaranteed two-way privacy at all times. Discuss samples under conditions similar to the intended room.</p></div><div><h3>Ready for the site.</h3><p>Identify the glazing type and any coatings or existing films before selecting a product. The responsible team should confirm whether the proposed design also meets the applicable visibility requirements.</p></details><details><summary>Can old film be removed?</summary><p>Removal can be discussed after checking the glass, film and access.
