with what the graphics need to do.</h2><p>A van that only needs to show who you are and how to reach you is a very different job from a van designed to be noticed across a car park. Before asking for a price, decide what the graphics must achieve. The answer sets the coverage, and coverage is the biggest single influence on cost.</p><p>A price quoted without that context is hard to judge. Tell us the make, model, wheelbase and roof height of the van, the colour it is painted and roughly what you want on it. Side and rear photographs help even more, because they show the panels, handles, windows and pressings the design has to work around.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="packages"><h2>What our published supply-and-fit packages include.</h2><p>For straightforward van lettering we publish three supply-and-fit packages, fitted within a 30-mile radius of our Norwich workshop. They are intended as a starting point for budgeting. The price for your particular van is confirmed by a quote once we know the vehicle and have seen your artwork.</p><p><strong>Basic graphics, from £149 + VAT.</strong> Single-colour cut vinyl of your company name to the bonnet, both side panels and the rear, with your web address and phone number on the lower side panels and the bottom of the rear doors.</p><p><strong>Standard graphics, from £210 + VAT.</strong> Everything in Basic, plus social media details, a second vinyl colour or a panel infill, and a cut or printed logo. The logo is subject to its complexity and to you having high-resolution files available.</p><p><strong>Pro graphics, from £455 + VAT.</strong> Everything in Basic and Standard, plus design options over and above regular graphic placement (up to three ideas) and a large logo or graphic element on the rear quarters and rear.</p><p>These packages are built around lettering and logos applied to the van’s existing paint colour. They are not full printed wraps. A wrap involves far more material, printing and fitting time, varies widely between vehicles and is quoted individually. If you are weighing the two approaches, our <a href="/vehicle-graphics/guides-and-advice/van-wrap-vs-part-graphics">van wrap vs part graphics comparison</a> sets out the differences.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="supply-only"><h2>Supply only: fitting the graphics yourself.</h2><p>If you are comfortable applying vinyl, or you are too far from Norwich for fitting to make sense, our <a href="/category/signage/vehicle-graphics">online shop</a> sells supply-only van graphics. Current shop prices start from £95 + VAT for Basic graphics on a small van, from £125 + VAT for Basic on a medium van, from £150 + VAT for Standard on a small van and from £225 + VAT for Standard on a medium van. There is also an online design builder on our <a href="/van-graphics">van graphics page</a> if you want to lay out your own design.</p><p>The saving is the fitting labour, and with it comes the responsibility for application. Vinyl needs a clean, dry, grease-free panel, a sensible temperature and patience with alignment. Be honest about the time and conditions you have before choosing self-fit purely on price.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="drivers"><h2>What moves a quote up or down.</h2><p><strong>Van size and coverage.</strong> A long-wheelbase, high-roof van has more panel area than a small car-derived van, so the same layout needs more vinyl and more fitting time. Adding panels, such as the roof line, rear quarters or bonnet, increases both.</p><p><strong>Cut or printed.</strong> Single-colour cut vinyl is the simplest route. Each extra colour is usually another layer to cut, weed and apply. Printed logos, gradients and photographs are produced on our 8-colour, 1440dpi printers and then cut to shape. We hold a large stock of coloured vinyl in-house, so a pre-coloured film is often the practical choice for solid lettering.</p><p><strong>Panel shape.</strong> Ribbed panels, rivets, deep pressings and sliding-door channels take longer to work around and can affect which film is suitable. Our <span>cast vs calendered vinyl guide</span> explains why.</p><p><strong>Old graphics.</strong> Removing existing vinyl adds time, and how long it takes is not always clear until the work starts. Older, sun-baked vinyl tends to come off in small pieces. Mention any existing graphics in your enquiry so they can be allowed for.</p><p><strong>Extras.</strong> Chapter 8 rear chevrons, reflective materials, window graphics and matching graphics for a trailer all add to the job. Ask for them in the same quote so the layouts can be planned together.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="artwork"><h2>Artwork is where hidden costs often sit.</h2><p>The Standard package includes a cut or printed logo on the condition that you can supply high-resolution files. That condition matters. A logo saved from a social media profile or a website header is usually too small and too soft to scale up to the side of a van. It may need redrawing before it can be cut or printed cleanly, and that is design time.</p><p>Ask whoever designed your logo for the original vector file, often supplied as AI, EPS, SVG or a vector PDF. If that is not available, our <a href="/design-home">in-house design department</a> can recreate it or design from scratch, and we will work with your own design team if you have one. Settle wording and phone numbers before approving the proof.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="fitting"><h2>Fitting, location and time off the road.</h2><p>Our supply-and-fit packages cover a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. If you are further out, you can bring the van to us, choose a posted self-install kit where the design is suitable, or ask for a quote for on-site fitting. Tell us your postcode at the start so the quote reflects the right option.</p><p>Time off the road is a real cost for a business that depends on its van. We have courtesy vehicles available while your van is with us, which is worth asking about when you book. Tell us about any recent paint repairs, as fresh paint can need time to cure before vinyl goes on.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="compare"><h2>How to compare van graphics quotes fairly.</h2><p>When you have more than one quote, line them up against the same specification. Check which panels are covered, how many colours are included, whether the logo is cut or printed, which brand and type of vinyl is specified, whether fitting is included and where it happens, whether removal of old graphics is included, how many design revisions are allowed and whether the figure includes VAT. Our prices are always shown + VAT.</p><p>Differences between quotes usually sit in the material, the coverage or the fitting. We use 3M and Metamark films. Ask any supplier to name the product so you can compare like with like. Our blog post on <a href="/blog/van-graphics-cost-compare-quotes-coverage">comparing van graphics quotes and coverage</a> goes into more detail.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="value"><h2>Think about cost per year, not just the invoice.</h2><p>Van graphics are semi-permanent. They can be updated, replaced or removed, and they will last up to 7 years if looked after correctly. Spread over the time you keep the van, a modest difference at the start becomes small. Our guide to <span>graphics on leased vans</span> covers that situation.</p><p>Illustrative example: a newly established electrician starts with Basic graphics on a white van, keeping the phone number on its own line. A year later the business adds a printed logo and a second colour without replacing the lettering already on the van. Another business might go straight to Pro so the rear carries a large logo from day one. The right budget follows the brief.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="checklist"><h2>Your project checklist.</h2><ul class="project-checklist"><li>Make, model, year, wheelbase and roof height of the van.</li><li>Side, rear and front photographs, including any existing graphics.</li><li>Your logo as a vector or high-resolution file, and the exact wording.</li><li>Which package you are considering, or a sketch of what you want where.</li><li>Your postcode and whether you want fitting, a posted kit or to visit us.</li><li>Any date you are working towards and whether you need a courtesy vehicle.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">TALK THROUGH YOUR PROJECT ↗</a></p></section><section class="reading-section" id="faq"><h2>Your questions. mainEntity.name: Do your van graphics prices include VAT?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. All of our published prices are shown + VAT and are “from” prices. The figure for your van is confirmed by a quote once we know the vehicle and have seen the artwork.

mainEntity.name: Does the Pro package include a full wrap?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Pro covers lettering, logos and extra design options, including a large logo or graphic element on the rear quarters and rear. Full and part wraps are quoted individually.

mainEntity.name: Can you fit the graphics if I am more than 30 miles from Norwich?

acceptedAnswer.text: The packages are fitted within a 30-mile radius. Further out, you can bring the van to our Norwich workshop, choose a posted self-install kit where suitable, or ask us to quote for on-site fitting.

mainEntity.name: I only have my logo as a JPEG. Is that a problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily, but a small or low-resolution image may need redrawing before it can be cut or printed cleanly. Send what you have and we will tell you whether it can be used as supplied.

mainEntity.name: Can I get a price from photographs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, photographs with the make and model are enough for an initial price. The quote is confirmed once the final layout and artwork are agreed.

class="reading-section" id="start"><h2>There are really three levels of coverage.</h2><p>People often frame the decision as a wrap or just some stickers. In practice there are three broad approaches. Cut vinyl graphics put lettering, logos and contact details on the van’s own paint. A part wrap covers a defined section, such as the rear half or the lower panels, with printed or coloured film. A full wrap covers most or all of the painted body, either with a printed design or a single colour-change film.</p><p>Each is a sensible choice for some businesses and an expensive mistake for others. The deciding factors are what the van needs to say, how long you will keep it, whether you own it and how much of your budget belongs on the vehicle rather than elsewhere in your marketing.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="at-a-glance"><h2>Compare at a glance.</h2><p class="table-hint">On a smaller screen, scroll across to compare all options.</p><div aria-label="Van wrap vs part graphics comparison table" class="comparison-scroll" role="region" tabindex="0"><table><caption>Van wrap vs part graphics at a glance</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Factor</th><th scope="col">Cut vinyl graphics</th><th scope="col">Part wrap</th><th scope="col">Full wrap</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Coverage</th><td>Lettering and logos on the paint</td><td>A planned section of the van</td><td>Most or all painted panels</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Appearance</th><td>Clean and clear; A clear company name, a short list of services, a phone number and a web address will tell people what they need to know. On a white van, a strong single colour is easy to read. A second colour, a panel infill or a printed logo adds character without the cost of covering whole panels.</p><p>Because the paint remains the background, design choices are mainly about hierarchy and spacing. Keep the name and number large enough to read from a distance and leave the panels uncluttered. This route also suits a business that expects details to change. A new phone number can be replaced as a single line of vinyl rather than a reprinted panel.</p><p>Our published supply-and-fit packages cover this approach. Basic starts from £149 + VAT, Standard from £210 + VAT and Pro from £455 + VAT, fitted within a 30-mile radius of our Norwich workshop and confirmed by a quote. See <a href="/vehicle-graphics/guides-and-advice/how-much-do-van-graphics-cost">how much van graphics cost</a> for what each includes.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="full"><h2>Full wraps: the van becomes the advert.</h2><p>A full wrap gives you the whole vehicle as a canvas. Photography, gradients, patterns and colours that run from bonnet to rear doors become possible, and the van can look nothing like the stock vehicle underneath. For a business where appearance is the product, such as a mobile café, a detailing service or an events company, that impact can be the point of the investment.</p><p>A wrap is also a bigger project. The design has to account for every door shut, handle, window, light and pressing, and the artwork must be planned so key elements are not lost across panel gaps. We produce mock-ups so you can see the design on your vehicle before anything is printed. Our printers produce prints roughly 1.5m wide by 50m long, so even large vehicles can be covered, and the film is chosen to suit the curves involved.</p><p>Wraps are quoted individually because the material, print and fitting time depend on the vehicle and the design. Ask for the quote to name the film and laminate so you know what you are paying for.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="part"><h2>The middle ground: a part wrap.</h2><p>A part wrap covers a planned section of the van, often the rear, the lower half or a band along each side. Combined with cut lettering on the remaining paint, it gives much of the visual impact of a full wrap with less material. It works best when the design treats the edge of the wrap as a deliberate line rather than an attempt to blend vinyl into paint.</p><p>Matching a vinyl colour exactly to a manufacturer’s paint colour is difficult, and the two can weather differently over time. Use the paint as a contrasting background, or choose a film colour that is clearly different. If your fleet includes vans in more than one paint colour, plan the part wrap so the design still looks consistent across them.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="practical"><h2>Repairs, removal and updates.</h2><p>Think about what happens after the van leaves the workshop. If a panel is damaged, cut lettering on that panel can usually be replaced on its own. With a wrap, the affected section is reprinted, so keep the approved artwork and the film details together.</p><p>Vinyl graphics are semi-permanent: they can be replaced or removed. Removal time depends on the coverage, the age of the film and the condition of the paint. Covering more of the van means more to remove later. Paint under a wrap is shaded from sunlight, while uncovered paint is not, so a faint outline can sometimes show after removal on older vehicles. If you lease the van, read our guide to <span>graphics on leased vans</span> before choosing.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="scenarios"><h2>Three examples of how the brief changes the choice.</h2><p>Illustrative example: a plumber with a new white panel van wants local customers to remember the name and number. A printed full wrap, designed around the serving hatch and the side that faces customers, does work that lettering cannot.</p><p>Illustrative example: a landscaping company runs several leased vans in different paint colours. A part wrap on the rear and lower panels with matching cut lettering keeps the fleet consistent, reduces the amount of film to remove at the end of each lease and still gives a strong presence on site.</p></section><section class="reading-section" id="alternatives"><h2>Other finishes worth knowing about.</h2><p>A colour-change wrap uses a single coloured or effect film rather than a print. Answered.</h2><details><summary>Is a full wrap always better than graphics?</summary><p>No. A wrap gives more visual impact, but clear lettering on the paint can be the better choice for a trade van that mainly needs to show a name and number. mainEntity.name: Is a full wrap always better than graphics?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A wrap gives more visual impact, but clear lettering on the paint can be the better choice for a trade van that mainly needs to show a name and number. Choose around what the van needs to do.

mainEntity.name: Can I start with graphics and add a wrap later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Graphics are semi-permanent, so lettering can be removed or reworked when you move to a wrap. Keep your artwork files so the new design can build on the old one.

mainEntity.name: Can you match vinyl to my van’s paint colour?

acceptedAnswer.text: An exact match is difficult, and paint and vinyl can age differently. A deliberate contrast usually looks better than a near match. We can show you film options at the design stage.

mainEntity.name: Does a wrap protect the paint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Vinyl covers the paint it sits on, but it is not a substitute for repairing damage. Paint condition affects both the fitting and the removal, so tell us about any repairs before work starts.

mainEntity.name: Which option is quickest to change if my details change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cut lettering on the paint, especially if contact details sit on their own line. On a printed wrap it depends where the details are placed, so plan them as a replaceable element.

That changes what the graphics need to do. Neighbours and passers-by see the van close up and at leisure, so a clear business name, a short list of services and a phone number that can be read from the pavement often matter more than a large, dramatic design.</p><p>On the move, the picture changes. Around the ring road and the routes in and out of the city, other drivers get a few seconds at most. A bold name on the sides and a simple, memorable rear do most of the work there. A good layout works in both.</p><p>Many Norwich vans belong to small trades businesses: electricians, plumbers, builders, roofers, landscapers, cleaners and property maintenance firms. mainEntity.name: Where is your workshop, and can I park there?

acceptedAnswer.text: We are at Vulcan House, Vulcan Road North, Norwich, NR6 6AQ, on the airport side of the city. Journey time depends on your starting point and traffic, so use the directions link for the current route. Call 01603 407786 before you arrive to discuss parking, particularly for a larger vehicle.

mainEntity.name: Can I have a courtesy vehicle while my van is with you?

acceptedAnswer.text: Courtesy vehicles are available while a van is off the road. Mention it when you book so we can check availability for your date.

mainEntity.name: Can you match graphics across a growing fleet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Working from the approved artwork for your first vehicles, a new van can be lettered to match the existing ones, even if it is a different make or size. Tell us about vehicles due for replacement so the layout can be planned to suit them.

mainEntity.name: Can graphics go on a leased or electric vehicle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, yes. Vinyl is semi-permanent and can be removed later, but check your lease or finance agreement first and tell us the terms. Electric vans and cars take graphics in the same way as any other vehicle.

mainEntity.name: Do I need my own design?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Our in-house design department can create a layout from scratch, or work from your existing logo and brand colours.

<section class="section" id="needs"><div class="wrap"><h2>Built for the working van.</h2><div class="local-article">
<p>For a plumber, electrician, builder or landscaper, the van is often the first thing a new customer sees: parked on a driveway all day, waiting outside a merchant first thing in the morning, or lined up on a site next to other contractors. Trade van graphics have a simple job. They say who you are, what you do and how to reach you, clearly enough for someone walking past or sitting behind you in traffic.</p>
<p>That usually means fewer words than people expect. A list of twelve services in small lettering is hard to read from the pavement. Your business name, a short line that describes the trade (“Plumbing & heating”, “Domestic electrical”, “Landscaping & driveways”), a phone number and a web address do most of the work. Extra detail belongs where people stand close to the van, such as the rear doors.</p>
<p>Trade vans also come with practical constraints. Roof racks and ladders hide the top of the side panels. Racking, ply-lining and rear steps change how the van is loaded and where people stand. Dents, scuffs and old signwriting may need dealing with first. We plan the layout around the van you actually drive rather than a clean diagram.</p>
</div></div></section>
<section class="section" id="placement"><div class="wrap"><h2>What goes where.</h2><div class="split picture"><figure><img alt="Smith Services van with company graphics on the side" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Smith-Services-Van-Graphics-jpg.webp"/></figure><div><span class="eyebrow">Layout</span><h3>Name high. Number low. Services short.</h3><p>Most trade layouts follow the same logic, because it matches how people see a van. The bonnet is read in mirrors and by oncoming traffic. The sides are seen from the pavement and the driveway. The rear doors get the longest look, from drivers stuck behind you at lights or in a queue, so they deserve the clearest phone number on the van.</p><div class="facts"><div><span>Bonnet</span><b>Business name</b></div><div><span>Side panels</span><b>Name, logo and a short trade line</b></div><div><span>Lower sides & rear doors</span><b>Phone number and web address</b></div></div><p>If ladders sit on the roof, keep key lettering below the rack line. On a sliding side door, we place lettering so the door still opens cleanly and nothing important falls across a handle or shut line.</p></div></div></div></section>
<section class="section" id="options"><div class="wrap"><h2>From basic lettering to a full wrap.</h2><p>Most tradespeople start with clear cut-vinyl lettering and add colour, a logo or printed panels as the business grows. These are our published supply-and-fit packages for vans fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. Every price is “from” and + VAT; your quote confirms the figure for your van.</p><div class="grid four">
<article class="card"><a href="/van-graphics"><img alt="RM Plastering van graphics" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/RM-Plastering-Vehicle-Graphics-jpg.avif"/></a><h3><a href="/van-graphics">Basic graphics, from £149 + VAT ↗</a></h3><p>Single-colour cut vinyl company name on the bonnet, both sides and rear, with phone and web address on the lower sides and bottom of the rear doors.</p></article>

Priced by quote for your vehicle and artwork.</p></article>
</div><p>Prefer to fit graphics yourself? Our <a href="/category/signage/vehicle-graphics">online shop</a> sells supply-only van graphics from £95 + VAT for a Basic small van, and the design builder lets you lay out your own. For a fuller breakdown, read <a href="/vehicle-graphics/guides-and-advice/how-much-do-van-graphics-cost">how much van graphics cost</a>.</p></div></section>
<section class="section tint" id="on-the-job"><div class="wrap"><h2>Practical points for working vans.</h2><div class="split picture"><div>
<p><b>Bodywork first.</b> Vinyl follows the surface it is applied to, so deep dents, flaking lacquer and poor repairs tend to show through. Graphics typically perform best on sound, original paint. Tell us about any repairs or previous signwriting when you send photographs.</p>
<p><b>Accreditation logos.</b> Customers look for the marks of schemes and trade bodies. Only include logos you are entitled to use, and check the scheme’s own rules on how its logo may be displayed. Send the official artwork files rather than a screenshot.</p>
<p><b>Leased or financed vans.</b> Check your agreement before booking. Our vehicle graphics are semi-permanent, so they can be removed or replaced, but your lease company may have its own conditions on graphics and return condition.</p>
<p><b>Time off the road.</b> We have courtesy vehicles available while your van is with us; ask about this when you book so the week’s jobs are not disrupted.</p>
</div><figure><img alt="Miller Installations van with vehicle graphics" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/miller-installations-7-scaled.webp"/></figure></div></div></section>
<section class="section" id="checklist"><div class="wrap"><h2>What to send us.</h2><p>A quick quote comes from good information. Before you get in touch, gather the following:</p><ul class="project-checklist"><li>The make, model and year of the van, plus wheelbase and roof height if you know them.</li><li>Photographs of both sides, the rear and the bonnet, including any ladders, racks or tow bars.</li><li>Your logo in the highest resolution you have; vector files are best.</li><li>The exact wording: business name, trade line, phone number, web address and social handles.</li><li>Any accreditation or supplier logos you want to show, in their official artwork.</li><li>Whether you want supply and fit, or a supply-only kit to fit yourself.</li></ul><p><a class="button purple" href="#enquiry">SEND YOUR VAN DETAILS ↗</a></p></div></section>
<section class="section tint" id="process"><div class="wrap"><h2>A clear process. From start to finish.</h2><div class="steps">
<article><img alt="Odd Job Mark van with full vehicle livery" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Odd-Job-Mark-Vehicle-Livery-jpg.avif"/><span class="number">01</span><h3>Tell us about the van.</h3><p>Send the photographs, wording and logo files. <article><img alt="Norfolk Exteriors van graphics" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/norfolk-exteriors-van-graphics-jpg.webp"/><span class="number">02</span><h3>Approve the layout.</h3><p>We lay the design out on your van model so you can check spelling, sizes and positions before anything is produced.</p></article>
<article><img alt="Window & Door Doctor van graphics" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/window-and-door-doctor-1-jpg.webp"/><span class="number">03</span><h3>Print and cut.</h3><p>Graphics are printed on our 8-colour, 1440dpi printers or cut from in-stock coloured vinyl, using 3M and Metamark materials.</p></article>
<article><img alt="Think Property van graphics" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/think-property-van-graphics-jpg.webp"/><span class="number">04</span><h3>Fit and hand back.</h3><p>We fit at our Norwich workshop and agree a date that suits your work. We will explain how to look after the graphics when you collect.</p></article>
</div></div></section>
<section class="section" id="faq"><div class="wrap"><h2>Your questions. Answered.</h2><div class="split picture"><div><figure><img alt="Miller Installations vehicle graphics, second view" loading="lazy" src="/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Miller-Installations-1.png"/></figure></div><div>
<details><summary>How much do trade van graphics cost?</summary><p>Our supply-and-fit packages start from £149 + VAT for Basic graphics, from £210 + VAT for Standard and from £455 + VAT for Pro, for vans fitted within 30 miles of our Norwich workshop. Wraps are quoted individually. The final price depends on the van and design, and is confirmed by quote.</p></details>
<details><summary>Will the graphics damage my paintwork when they come off?</summary><p>Vehicle graphics are semi-permanent and designed to be removed. On sound factory paint, quality vinyl usually comes away cleanly. Resprayed or damaged areas carry more risk, so mention any previous repairs when you ask for a quote.</p></details>
<details><summary>How long will the graphics last?</summary><p>Using 3M and Metamark materials, our van graphics will last up to 7 years if looked after correctly. Regular hand washing and avoiding harsh chemicals or aggressive pressure washing at the edges help them last.</p></details>
<details><summary>I’ve added a new service. Do I need all-new graphics?</summary><p>Not necessarily. Because the vinyl is semi-permanent, individual lines such as a phone number or service list can be removed and replaced quickly, leaving the rest of the van as it is.</p></details>
<details><summary>Can I keep working while my van is being done?</summary><p>We have courtesy vehicles available while a van is off the road. Ask when you book so we can check availability for your dates.</p></details>
</div></div></div></section>
